Qwen.content:
Skip to content

# Apple’s China AI partner has had a rough ride

Editor’s note: On Nov. 4, Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China, with Alibaba’s Qwen available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence experiences. The partnership crowns an unusually fast ascent for a model family launched in 2023. Hugging Face counted more than 2 billion Qwen downloads on its own Hub in the first seven months of 2026, well ahead of Google and Meta. But Qwen’s rise was anything but smooth: internal skepticism, fierce competition and senior departures shaped the model long before it became a global name.

First, Qwen Had to Win at Home

Qwen’s path to Apple did not begin as the story of an inevitable champion.

Alibaba introduced Tongyi Qianwen in April 2023, months after ChatGPT jolted China’s technology industry into a race to build large language models. It soon began releasing model weights publicly, gradually making open source central to Qwen’s strategy.

Even inside Alibaba, Qwen was not the automatic choice. Some teams kept using Meta’s Llama well into 2024, while Fliggy and Alibaba.com later experimented with DeepSeek’s R1. The model had to win over its own company before it could win over the wider market.

Open source became part of the answer. Developers fine-tuned Qwen, built derivatives and fed improvements back to the team, which credited that feedback in Qwen2.5’s expansion across language, coding and mathematics.

By late 2024, Qwen2.5 had begun winning over developers in China and the US — and more teams inside Alibaba.

Then DeepSeek arrived. Its R1 reasoning model raised the stakes across China’s AI industry, putting new pressure on rivals to deliver stronger reasoning at lower cost.

Alibaba founder Jack Ma repeatedly asked executives for updates on its development, according to The Information. In the final sprint, mattresses appeared beneath desks for power naps; some employees slept only a handful of hours during the final week.

Qwen3, released in April 2025, pushed into that new battleground with eight open models and hybrid reasoning, switching between a slower “thinking” mode for complex tasks and faster responses when deeper reasoning was unnecessary.

Its largest open model used a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating just 22 billion of 235 billion parameters at a time to cut inference costs. Reuters framed the launch as part of an intensifying Chinese AI race following DeepSeek’s rise.

### Qwen’s Next Challenge Was Inside the Team

Over the next year, Qwen kept expanding its model family and developer reach. But by early 2026, the pressure around the team was no longer just technical.

In March, technical leader Junyang Lin abruptly announced his departure with three words: “Bye my beloved Qwen.” Post-training chief Bowen Yu also left, following senior researcher Binyuan Hui earlier that year.

Alibaba didn’t publicly detail Lin’s reasons. 36Kr reported tensions over a proposed reorganization, team boundaries, hiring and computing resources.

At an emergency all-hands meeting, researchers questioned why paying Alibaba Cloud customers could secure computing capacity while Qwen’s own team remained short of resources.

Management acknowledged communication problems while saying the changes were meant to strengthen, not weaken, Qwen.

The episode pointed to a broader tension facing frontier AI labs: cutting-edge models demand centralized capital and vast computing resources, while top research teams often rely on autonomy and fast decision-making.

Alibaba responded by tightening coordination. In June, it created Token Foundry, consolidating key model-development teams under CEO Eddie Wu.

By September, longtime Qwen researcher Dayiheng Liu had been appointed head of the Qwen large language model project, bringing more clarity after several rounds of reorganization.

### Beyond the Model Race

Qwen had grown beyond a model family into a broader stack: foundation models for language, coding and multimodal tasks; Alibaba Cloud’s Model Studio for developers and enterprises; and consumer products such as the Qwen App.

That breadth mattered to Apple. After evaluating Chinese AI providers including Baidu, Tencent, ByteDance, Alibaba and DeepSeek, Apple chose Alibaba as a partner for Apple Intelligence in China.

By August 2026, Apple had also trained a China-specific model with Alibaba’s support, while the approved setup incorporated Qwen.

Its broader AI investment strategy also covers foundation models and AI-native applications, as well as integrating AI across existing businesses. By May 2026, Alibaba said its spending would exceed the original 380 billion yuan plan.

The Apple deal marks a new phase. The harder part may be keeping Qwen fast, focused and inventive as the machinery around it gets bigger.

DragonLab cuts through the noise to find the Chinese startups, founders, and technologies that could shape what comes next.

Have a startup we should know about? Reach us at dragonlab@technode.com.

Qwen.content:
# 不抢商品抢 Token，阿里 AI 能翻盘吗？

蓝洞商业·2026年11月06日 21:26

Token 好卖，留存待考

今年的双 11，阿里最忙的似乎不再是电商，而是年轻的 ATH 事业群。

先是 11 月 2 日晚，千问办公 CEO 陈宇森坐进了李佳琦直播间，原价 28 元/月的千问办公基础版月卡以 0.01 元上架，半小时卖出 10 万份，对应约 2 万亿 Token。

这是千问办公的一个破圈行动，让 Token 从模型计费单位，变成了货架商品。

然后是 11 月 4 日，国行版 Apple Intelligence（苹果智能）首次开放测试，千问接入国行苹果智能，在Siri、写作工具和视觉智能等入口中提供文本与图像理解能力，而更多的中国用户要等到 12 月 iOS 27.3 正式发布时，才能体验到这一延迟两年落地的功能。

这是一份迟到的落地，在苹果智能的设置中，对应的能力开关是千问 App。

而更值得期待的模型是最新一代的 Qwen4，包含Qwen4 Max、Flash、Plus 和 27B四个版本，距离 9 月杭州的云栖大会上刘大一恒做出的预告，已经过去了一个多月，而网传 Qwen4 即将在 11 月初发布，目前Qwen4 架构已经适配华为昇腾。面向未来的竞争，Qwen4.5 和 Qwen 5预计扩到 5 万亿到 10 万亿参数。

参数越大，投入的资源和成本就越高，10 万亿参数，是阿里、字节和 DeepSeek 公开竞逐的模型目标路线。

直播间卖 Token，接入苹果智能，发参数更大的模型，这三件事组合起来就是今年双 11 的 AI 浓度，恰好对应的是阿里 ATH 事业群中的三个核心业务：

第一，千问办公负责 AI to B端，与 WorkBuddy、豆包工作抢市场，直播间卖 Token 是一次引流大促；

第二，千问事业部负责 AI to C 端，接入苹果智能后，千问要接受苹果手机用户的使用和挑剔，并收获用户增长；

第三，Qwen4 将成为阿里 Token Foundry 成立后的首个完整模型家族，也是刘大一恒接替林俊旸、执掌 Qwen LLM 的核心职责后拿出的首个成绩单。

阿里最年轻的ATH事业群，自今年 3 月成立以来，已经经历至少 4 轮变革，包括 6 月成立吴泳铭直管的 Token Foundry、陈宇森出任千问办公负责人，以及 7 月张迪接管通义万相团队等，每次变阵，都是在解决一个决策瓶颈，这是互联网大厂中绝无仅有的。

刘大一恒、陈宇森等年轻的阿里人，正从技术与产品骨干走向阿里 AI 体系的关键执行位置，组织上的变化是否带来能力上的闭环，以及效率的最优解？

所以，这个 AI 浓度很高的双 11，也将成为检验阿里 AI 组织变革成效的节点，长远来看，模型竞争力转化为稳定的客户付费，最终能否形成B 端与 C端的业务协同。

## 「残血」苹果，「满血」千问？

今年 6 月，能读屏、跨 App 执行的新一代 Siri AI 发布，但国行苹果智能的水平还停留在两年前。彭博的消息显示，「苹果高管并不乐观地认为 Siri AI 短期内会在中国推出」。

国行苹果智能首批开放的功能，主要包括实时翻译、写作工具、视觉智能、照片消除等，但为了遵守相关规定，苹果在中国推出的首个智能助手版本，将缺少苹果自主研发的图像生成工具，包括 Image Playground 应用。

这意味着苹果智能落地中国市场，注定是一个「残血版本」，目前苹果手机的 AI 功能，大都是国产安卓手机早已成熟的功能。但戏剧性恰恰在于，「残血」的几乎都是苹果自研功能，「满血」的是合作方千问的能力。

千问在苹果手机中的场景，主要是接入苹果 Siri、写作工具和视觉智能三个系统级入口：

第一，设置千问账号后，按住侧边键调用 Siri，Siri 答不上来的复杂问题，会先弹窗征求同意，再转给千问，回答旁边标着「千问」和来源数量，点一下就能跳进千问 App 接着聊；

第二，在写作工具中，苹果原生的工具提供校对、摘要和格式整理等功能，而要从零开始创作，则会调用千问的「自由创作」能力，生成文章、邮件和图片等；

第三，在视觉智能中，用户可以通过 iPhone 摄像头识别眼前的物体和场景，当用户提出问题，会覆盖「询问」「翻译」「搜索」三个场景。唯一不调用千问能力的是「搜索」，由百度识图默认提供支持，能够根据镜头画面搜索类似图片。

从目前的测试报道看，采用端侧与云端协同的架构：简单任务可在设备本地处理；对于部分复杂问答或创作请求，系统会提示用户是否调用千问的云端能力。这意味着「残血」的苹果智能，用「满血」的千问来补足能力。但要注意，如果用户不主动开启千问功能，苹果系统不会自动转接。

这对阿里千问来说，当然是一个利好的起点，它借此进入苹果智能的交互流程、获得系统级曝光，只是这套流程仍由苹果掌控。

与此同时，这也对千问带来了体验端的压力：苹果手机用户是否愿意启用千问，调用过程是否足够顺畅，回答质量能否达到预期，敏感内容和附件的处理方式是否清楚，这都是苹果智能正式版需要不断优化和提高的地方，而更值得观察的点在于，未来阿里与苹果是否披露可验证的用户量或兑现的商业价值。

千问 App 月活量目前位居行业第二，QuestMobile 数据显示，2026年 9 月，千问 App 月活跃用户规模为 1.58 亿，第一名豆包月活为4.19 亿，第三名的位置是 DeepSeek，月活为 1.2 亿。

在月均使用次数和使用时长上，千问明显低于豆包和 DeepSeek。2026 年 9 月，豆包和 DeepSeek 人均使用次数分别为 72 次和 65.9 次，而千问仅为 17.8 次，在月均使用时长上，千问的 22.7 分钟，也明显低于 DeepSeek、豆包、元宝、Kimi 和文心。

千问能否借助苹果智能大幅提升用户使用时长和使用次数？千问能否变成苹果手机用户愿意信任也愿意反复使用的能力？这都是苹果智能正式版需要兑现的价值点，苹果和千问都得到了一块彼此需要的拼图，但目前它还不是完整答案。

## Token 好卖，留存待考

今年双 11，在淘宝千问办公官方旗舰店，一共有三个商品： 0.01 元的千问办公基础版会员月卡， 1169 元的千问办公 A2 听记卡，869 元的千问办公桌面机器人。截至目前，会员月卡销量 10 万+，两款硬件销量 1000+。

当千问办公 CEO 陈宇森坐进了李佳琦直播间，原价 28 元每月的千问办公基础版月卡以 0.01 元上架，半小时卖出 10 万份，这场低价体验和获客活动就已经实现了拉新用户的目的。

1 分钱是企业办公 Agent 极低的试用门槛，对阿里来说，把用户带进「付款—兑换—完成任务」的链路中，但不意味着用户买到了更多的 Token，对用户来说，豆包工作 30 天免费期，WorkBuddy 每月 500 积分，都是可领取的免费权益。

真正考验千问办公的，要看用户在首月之后是否继续使用和付费，毕竟办公 Agent 的商业模式是售卖交付结果。

目前企业办公类 Agent 付费率尚无权威统计数据，参照部分 AI 原生 App 的月度付费活跃比例，千问办公个人端付费率可暂设 5%—15% 作情景测算，但办公类 Agent 主流套餐，是按组织席位收费，或是按 Token 管理收费，即便是 WorkBuddy 目前的付费率也不能覆盖成本。

千问办公在用户规模上位居行业第三。 QuestMobile 数据显示，截至2026 年 9 月，在 PC 与移动端五类形态下，AI 办公月活规模达 1.42 亿，同比增长 50.6%，其中 WorkBuddy、百度搭子、千问办公规模分别为 3235.3 万、977 万、790.5 万，腾讯 WorkBuddy 领先优势明显。

事实上，790.5 万不能直接代表千问办公的总触达或总使用规模，该口径未统计钉钉 App 及 PC 客户端内的千问办公使用量，而 9 月初千问办公官方披露的数据口径，千问办公上线满一个月，用户数突破 3000 万，企业用户占比超过一半。

只能代表 Agent 办公的阶段性渗透，真正的商业化竞争还处于初期。《财新》10 月份报道，WorkBuddy 处于行业领先，但产品本身变现能力有限，接入大量外部模型，Token 调用花费要向模型厂商结算，「本质上还是亏本生意」。

而在 Agent 能力上，千问办公目前也处于「中等生」水平。

《第一财经》测试了千问办公、WorkBuddy 和豆包工作三款产品，核心发现之一是：使用三款产品的基本套餐，豆包工作的积分消耗速度最快，其次是千问办公，WorkBuddy 的积分最经用，而且千问办公积分消耗在于，「它是财报分析中数据错误最多的」。

## 模型走到了年末结算期

2026 年下半年，大模型行业完成了一次安静的叙事切换，国产旗舰模型的更新节奏明显放缓。

一个重要的原因是，市场更关注的是模型能力，而不只是模型的评测分数。模型的 Token 消耗，成为衡量模型带来的实际价值之一，所以更有性价比的 flash 版模型成为很大的关注点，近期腾讯发布的 Hy4 带来能力提升，而能大幅降低成本的 Hy4 Flash 版本更受期待。

而另外一个趋势是，中国模型公司在开放权重路线上更占优势，这也让 Qwen4 成为下半年国产阵营留下的最大悬念。

阿里和腾讯都是模型开放权重阵营的核心玩家，腾讯作为模型能力上的追赶者，近期已经交卷了 Hy4，追赶速度很快，Hy4 Preview 于 8 月 28 日发布，Hy4 于11月4日正式发布，相隔约 68 天。而从阿里 Qwen4的节奏看，从 Qwen3.8-Max 到下一代旗舰 Qwen4，已经过去约三个月。

Qwen4 等待时间长不代表阿里落后了，毕竟阿里要发的是全尺寸矩阵模型，而不是单一旗舰模型。尤其是行业中最为期待的 27B 版本，可能成为差异化竞争的关键。

每一代模型都有自己不同的竞争点，腾讯 Hy4 就进一步增强了指令遵循、长文本理解和长程 Agent 能力，并首次加入视觉理解与电脑操作：模型能分析图表、图片等内容，也能结合命令行和图形界面完成操作任务，这让 Hy4 的竞争重点落在长任务执行、办公与编程场景，以及模型到产品的接入上，这天然利好的是 WorkBuddy 等应用。

反观 Qwen4，它已积累多年的开发者与衍生模型生态，海外市场关注 27B版本的原因，也正是因为其如果能力足够强、权重开放、量化和推理支持成熟，就有机会进入更多企业私有化环境中，让开发者工作站、中小团队出海更具竞争优势。

当然，Qwen4 旗舰模型必然会与行业对手进行正面竞争。目前，「最大开源模型」的位置，由总参数约 2.8T 的 Kimi K3.1 Pro占据，Qwen4 Max 能否改写这一格局吗？这个双 11，阿里会给出答案。

Qwen.content:
# What Is Qwen? Alibaba's AI Models Explained

Qwen is Alibaba's AI model family. The Qwen3.8 lineup, how its licenses differ, how to try it, and what Alibaba has said about Qwen 4.

Qwen is the family of AI models built by Alibaba. If you have seen a model name like Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen3.8-27B or Qwen-Image-2.1, it comes from the same team. Some Qwen models are offered through Alibaba's cloud API. Others have weights you can download and run on your own hardware.

This guide explains what Qwen is, what is in the current lineup, how the licenses differ, how to try the models, and what Alibaba has said about Qwen 4. Facts are as of November 4, 2026. For how Qwen fits next to DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and other Chinese labs, see our guide to China's AI labs.

## Who makes Qwen

Qwen models are published under the Qwen organization on Hugging Face and the QwenLM organization on GitHub. The research license on one Qwen model names the legal entity behind it. The Qwen-Image-2.1 license defines "We" as "Hangzhou Tongyi Laboratory Technology Co., Ltd."

Alibaba presents Qwen as part of a larger plan. In its September 22, 2026 Apsara Conference press release, Alibaba described updates "featuring Qwen foundation models and multimodal models, new proprietary AI chips, a purpose-built agentic cloud, and an AI agent platform for mobile phones."

## The current lineup

Qwen is not one model. It is several product lines that share a name. The main text models today belong to the Qwen3.8 generation. The diagram below shows the three Qwen3.8 text models with published weights, using the sizes and licenses from each model card.

### Qwen3.8-Max and its open weights

Qwen3.8-Max is the flagship. Alibaba published the open weights behind it as Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, uploaded to Hugging Face on August 8, 2026 (UTC). The model card lists "2.4T in total and 95B activated" parameters.

The model card says: "For the first time, Qwen3.8 brings a Qwen-Max-class model to open release." It also says the hosted version is different from the download: "Qwen3.8-Max is the official version based on Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B with more features, such as vision input & non-thinking support, 1M context length by default, official built-in tools, etc."

The Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-Max describes it as a "2.4-trillion-parameter MoE flagship" and lists image, text and video as inputs and text as output.

### Qwen3.8-27B

Qwen3.8-27B is the compact dense model, uploaded on August 5, 2026 (UTC). Its model card calls it "a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control." The card lists 27B parameters.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was uploaded on August 24, 2026 (UTC). Its model card lists "125B with 6B activated, plus 51B n-gram embedding and 4B MTP" parameters. The card calls it an "experimental preview of the architecture that will underpin Qwen4." It also says the hosted Qwen3.8-Flash is "the official version based on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with more production features."

The card names four changes in this architecture: hybrid attention with Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA), a "Gated Residual" design, n-gram embeddings, and a training recipe that applies the Muon and AdamW optimizers to different weight categories.

### Image models

Qwen also makes image models. The main image model on the Qwen Hugging Face page is Qwen-Image-2.1, uploaded on September 14, 2026 (UTC). Its card describes "a unified text-to-image generation and image editing model" with "7B parameters in its visual generation component." The card says it can make transparent (RGBA) images and supports "up to 10 reference images" for editing. A faster variant, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, followed on October 9, 2026 (UTC). Alibaba's September 22 press release says Qwen-Image 3.1 is "set to launch later this year."

## Open weights do not all mean the same license

Each Qwen model has its own license, and they are not the same. Always read the LICENSE file in the repository you download.

- Qwen3.8-27B: Apache 2.0. The model card metadata listslicense: apache-2.0.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: Qwen Community License 1.0. The LICENSE file has two conditions. The first says that if the model is used for commercial products or services "that have more than 100,000,000 monthly active users or US$ 20,000,000 (or equivalent in other currencies) monthly revenue, respective model name must be prominently displayed on the user interface of such product or service." The second says: "If the licensee or any of its affiliates conducts a Model as a Service or AI Work Assistant business, the licensee shall obtain a separate license from Qwen before Using the Software or its derivative works for any commercial purpose." It adds: "The foregoing requirement shall not apply to the licensee's internal Use of the Software, provided that such Use does not make the Software, its outputs, or its underlying model capabilities available to any third party."
- Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B: Qwen3.8-Max License. The LICENSE file has the same first condition. Its second condition adds a revenue trigger: "If the licensee or any of its affiliates conducts a Model as a Service or AI Work Assistant business, and the aggregate revenue of the licensee and its affiliates exceeds US$50,000,000 (or the equivalent amount in any other currencies) during any consecutive twelve (12) months, the licensee shall obtain a separate license from Qwen before Using the Software or its derivative works for any commercial purpose." The same internal-use exception follows.
- Qwen-Image-2.1: Qwen Research License Agreement. The LICENSE file is a separate agreement dated September 20, 2026. It grants rights "for non-commercial purposes only" and says commercial use needs a separate license from Qwen.

Both the Community License and the Qwen3.8-Max License define the two business types. "Model as a Service" means "giving a third party access to language model inference or fine-tuning (e.g., via API or a hosted endpoint) in a manner that allows such third parties to exercise meaningful control over the inputs, parameters, or training data." "AI Work Assistant" means "an independent AI-powered product primarily designed for AI-assisted coding or office productivity (e.g., Qoder and QwenWork)."

This guide does not give legal advice. If you plan to build a product on a Qwen model, have a lawyer read the license for that exact model.

## How to try Qwen

There are three main ways to use Qwen, depending on what you want.

- Chat in a browser. The Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B model card has a Qwen Studio button that links to Qwen's chat site, chat.qwen.ai. The Qwen Hugging Face page calls the same site Qwen Chat.
- Call the API. The model cards say: "the official Qwen API service is provided by Qwen Cloud." Each model has its own page, such as Qwen3.8-Flash, with features, rate limits and pricing. The Qwen3.8-Max page lists features including function calling, structured outputs, batches, web search and fine-tuning. Prices change, so check the model page before you build.
- Download the weights. Open-weight models are on Hugging Face. The model cards say the files work with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang and TokenSpeed (the 2.4T card lists vLLM, SGLang and TokenSpeed).

Note that the hosted and downloaded versions are not always the same. For both Max and Flash, the model cards say the hosted "official version" adds features such as a 1M context length by default and built-in tools.

## Qwen 4: what Alibaba has said

Alibaba's September 22, 2026 press release says: "At the conference, Alibaba revealed that its next-generation model, Qwen 4, is currently in training." It adds: "The company further announced its roadmap for the upcoming Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 model series, projected to scale up to 5 to 10 trillion parameters."

The same release reports a self-improvement test. Alibaba says that over a month of fully automated runs, Qwen3.8-Max "completed 33 iterative cycles," and that "the updated Qwen3.8-Max boosted its Artificial Analysis score from 40 to 45." Those are Alibaba's figures, published September 22, 2026.

On October 29, 2026, an attendee at Alibaba's Apsara event in Amsterdam posted that Qwen 4 would come "next week." We covered that report in Qwen4 Next Week? What Alibaba Said in Amsterdam. As of November 4, 2026, the Qwen organization on Hugging Face listed no Qwen 4 model. The newest upload was Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, from October 9, 2026 (UTC).

## Why Qwen matters

Alibaba offers its Qwen flagship as a hosted API and has also published downloadable weights at several sizes, from a 27B dense model to the 2.4T-parameter model that Qwen3.8-Max is based on. Users can call the API, or run the weights under the license for that model.

A model being downloadable does not mean every use is free of conditions. Apache 2.0 on the 27B model and the Community License on Flash-Next have different rules for the same kind of business. For a closer look at the Qwen3.8 release itself, see our Qwen3.8 explainer.

## Quick answers

Is Qwen open source? Some Qwen models have downloadable weights, but the licenses differ. Qwen3.8-27B uses Apache 2.0. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses the Qwen Community License 1.0, and the 2.4T model uses the Qwen3.8-Max License, both with the conditions quoted above. Qwen-Image-2.1 uses the Qwen Research License Agreement, which is for non-commercial use only.

Is the downloaded Qwen3.8-Max the same as the API version? No. The model card says the hosted Qwen3.8-Max adds "vision input & non-thinking support, 1M context length by default, official built-in tools, etc." over the downloadable Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B.

Can Qwen models see images? The Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cards list the type as "Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder." The Qwen Cloud page lists image, text and video as inputs for Qwen3.8-Max.

Has Qwen 4 been released? Not as of November 4, 2026. Alibaba's latest written statement on Qwen 4 tha

Qwen.content:
# Alibaba Cloud (Qwen)

Alibaba Cloud's DashScope API provides OpenAI-compatible access to Qwen language models. Use OpenAI provider options supported by your chosen model.

## Setup

To use Alibaba Cloud's API, set theDASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file:
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI provider options; support varies by model. Example:
providers:
  - alibaba:qwen3.8-max # Simple usage
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.7-plus # Aliases: alicloud:, aliyun:, dashscope:
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to DASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable
      apiBaseUrl: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 # Optional: Override default API base URL

note

The equivalent provider prefixes arealicloud:, aliyun:, and dashscope:. For new configurations, Alibaba recommends qwen3.7-plus for balanced use, qwen3.8-flash for lower cost, or qwen3.8-max for stronger reasoning. Check the model catalog for your region; model availability differs by region.

If you're using the Alibaba Cloud Beijing region console, switch the base URL tohttps://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 instead of the international endpoint.

## Supported Models

The built-in Alibaba provider implements OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and text embeddings. The catalog below also lists separate realtime, speech recognition, and image generation services. Listing a model here does not add those endpoints to this provider. Choose a model supported by your selected endpoint and region.

### Qwen 3 Flagship

- qwen3.8-max / qwen3.8-max-0902 - Current flagship with text, image, and video input and a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.8-flash - Faster Qwen3.8 model with a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.7-plus / qwen3.7-plus-2026-05-26 - General-purpose model with thinking, vision, and tool calling
- qwen3.7-flash / qwen3.7-flash-2026-07-15 - Lower-cost Qwen3.7 model
- qwen3.7-max / qwen3.7-max-2026-06-08 - Previous flagship
- qwen3.6-plus / qwen3.6-flash and qwen3.5-plus / qwen3.5-flash - Previous model families
- qwen3-max - Supports reasoning and tool calling
- qwen3-max-preview - Preview version with thinking mode support
- qwen3-max-2025-09-23 - September 2025 snapshot
- qwen-max - 32K context (30,720 in, 8,192 out)
- qwen-max-latest - Always updated to latest version
- qwen-max-2025-01-25 - January 2025 snapshot
- qwen-plus / qwen-plus-latest - 128K-1M context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen-plus-2025-09-11, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-plus-2025-07-14, qwen-plus-2025-04-28, qwen-plus-2025-01-25 - Dated snapshots
- qwen-flash / qwen-flash-2025-07-28 - Latency-optimized general model
- qwen-turbo / qwen-turbo-latest / qwen-turbo-2025-04-28 / qwen-turbo-2024-11-01 - Earlier low-latency model; see qwen-flash
- qwen-long-latest / qwen-long-2025-01-25 - 10M context for long-text analysis, summarization, and extraction

### Qwen 3 Omni & Realtime

- qwen3.8-omni-flash - Text output from text, image, audio, and video input through Chat Completions; use the separate realtime API for qwen3.8-omni-flash-realtime
- qwen3-omni-flash / qwen3-omni-flash-2025-09-15 - Supports speech and vision in thinking and non-thinking modes
- qwen3-omni-flash-realtime / qwen3-omni-flash-realtime-2025-09-15 - Streaming realtime with audio stream input and VAD
- qwen3-omni-30b-a3b-captioner - Dedicated audio captioning model (speech, ambient sounds, music)
- qwen2.5-omni-7b - Qwen2.5-based multimodal model with text, image, speech, and video inputs

### Reasoning & Research

- qwq-plus - Alibaba's reasoning model (commercial)
- qwq-32b - Open-source QwQ reasoning model trained on Qwen2.5
- qwq-32b-preview - Experimental QwQ research model (2024)
- qwen-deep-research - Long-form research assistant with web search
- qvq-max / qvq-max-latest / qvq-max-2025-03-25 - Visual reasoning models (commercial)
- qvq-72b-preview - Experimental visual reasoning research model
- DeepSeek models (hosted by Alibaba Cloud):
- deepseek-v4.1-flash / deepseek-v4-pro-0813 - Current hosted Flash and Pro models; these IDs differ from the direct DeepSeek API
- deepseek-v3.2-exp / deepseek-v3.1 / deepseek-v3 - DeepSeek V3 models
- deepseek-r1 / deepseek-r1-0528 - DeepSeek reasoning models
- deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-{1.5b,7b,14b,32b} - Distilled on Qwen2.5
- deepseek-r1-distill-llama-{8b,70b} - Distilled on Llama

### Vision & Multimodal

Commercial:

- qwen3-vl-plus / qwen3-vl-plus-2025-09-23 - High-res image support with long context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen3-vl-flash / qwen3-vl-flash-2025-10-15 - Fast vision model with thinking mode support
- qwen-vl-max - 7.5K context, 1,280 tokens/image
- qwen-vl-plus - High-res image support
- qwen-vl-ocr - OCR-optimized for documents, tables, handwriting (30+ languages)

Open-source:

- qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-thinking / qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct - 235B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-32b-thinking / qwen3-vl-32b-instruct - 32B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-thinking / qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-instruct - 30B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-8b-thinking / qwen3-vl-8b-instruct - 8B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen2.5-vl-{72b,7b,3b}-instruct - Qwen 2.5 VL series

### Audio & Speech

- qwen3-asr-flash / qwen3-asr-flash-2025-09-08 - Multilingual speech recognition (11 languages, Chinese dialects)
- qwen3-asr-flash-realtime / qwen3-asr-flash-realtime-2025-10-27 - Real-time speech recognition with automatic language detection
- qwen3-omni-flash-realtime - Supports speech streaming with VAD

### Coding & Math

Commercial:

- qwen3-coder-plus / qwen3-coder-plus-2025-09-23 / qwen3-coder-plus-2025-07-22 - Coding agents with tool calling
- qwen3-coder-flash / qwen3-coder-flash-2025-07-28 - Fast code generation
- qwen-math-plus / qwen-math-plus-latest / qwen-math-plus-2024-09-19 / qwen-math-plus-2024-08-16 - Math problem solving
- qwen-math-turbo / qwen-math-turbo-latest / qwen-math-turbo-2024-09-19 - Fast math reasoning
- qwen-mt-{plus,turbo} - Machine translation (92 languages)
- qwen-doc-turbo - Document mining and structured extraction

Open-source:

- qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct / qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct - Open-source Qwen3 coder models
- qwen2.5-math-{72b,7b,1.5b}-instruct - Math-focused models with CoT/PoT/TIR reasoning

### Qwen 2.5 Series

All support 131K context (129,024 in, 8,192 out)

- qwen2.5-{72b,32b,14b,7b}-instruct
- qwen2.5-{7b,14b}-instruct-1m

### Qwen 2 Series

- qwen2-72b-instruct - 131K context
- qwen2-57b-a14b-instruct - 65K context
- qwen2-7b-instruct - 131K context

### Qwen 1.5 Series

8K context (6K in, 2K out)

- qwen1.5-{110b,72b,32b,14b,7b}-chat

### Qwen 3 Open-source Models

Open-source Qwen3 models with thinking mode support:

- qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking / qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct - Next-gen 80B (September 2025)
- qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507 / qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 - 235B July 2025 versions
- qwen3-30b-a3b-thinking-2507 / qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507 - 30B July 2025 versions
- qwen3-235b-a22b - 235B with dual-mode support (thinking/non-thinking)
- qwen3-32b - 32B dual-mode model
- qwen3-30b-a3b - 30B dual-mode model
- qwen3-14b, qwen3-8b, qwen3-4b - Smaller dual-mode models
- qwen3-1.7b, qwen3-0.6b - Edge/mobile models

### Third-party Models

Kimi (Moonshot AI):

- kimi-k3 - Current Kimi model
- kimi-k2.6 - Previous Kimi model with a 256K context window
- moonshot-kimi-k2-instruct - First open-source trillion-parameter MoE model in China (activates 32B parameters)

Z.AI (GLM):ZHIPU/GLM-5.3 and glm-5.2. Check the regional model catalog for access and endpoint requirements.

### Embeddings

Usealibaba:embedding:<model> for embeddings. The alibaba:<model> shorthand sends chat requests.

- text-embedding-v3 - 1,024d vectors, 8,192 token limit, 50+ languages
- text-embedding-v4 - Latest Qwen3-Embedding with flexible dimensions (64-2048d), 100+ languages
- qwen3.7-text-embedding - Newer Qwen3.7 text embeddings; availability depends on the region

defaultTest:
  options:
    provider:
      embedding:
        id: alibaba:embedding:text-embedding-v4

### Image Generation

Thealibaba provider does not call image-generation endpoints. To use models such as qwen-image-plus, configure the HTTP provider for Alibaba's image API.

See the DashScope model catalog for availability.

## Additional Configuration

Put DashScope-specific request fields underconfig.passthrough. For example, enable_thinking controls thinking mode on Qwen3.8 and Qwen3.7 chat models:
providers:
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.8-max
    config:
      passthrough:
        enable_thinking: true

Standard OpenAI parameters (temperature, max_tokens) are supported. Base URL:https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 (or https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 for the Beijing region).

For API usage details, see Alibaba Cloud documentation.

# China’s AI models, led by Kimi, dominate open-source enterprise spending

Chinese systems account for 89 per cent of spending on open-source models, but the category is small compared with spending on proprietary models

2-MIN READ2-MIN

0

Minxiao Changin Shenzhen

Chinese artificial intelligence models led by Moonshot AI’s Kimi family accounted for nearly nine-tenths of estimated global enterprise spending on open-source systems, according to a new study, even though proprietary US rivals continue to capture the vast majority of overall revenue.

The report, released this week by Silicon Valley venture capital firm Menlo Ventures, said Chinese AI systems accounted for 89 per cent of global enterprise spending on open-source models. Kimi led with a 61 per cent share, followed by DeepSeek at 15 per cent and Z.ai’s GLM series at 11 per cent.

By contrast, Meta Platforms’ Llama series, the leading Western offering in the category, accounted for just 7 per cent of open-source enterprise spending.

The global numbers were extrapolated from a September survey of nearly 400 US enterprise decision-makers managing more than US$4 billion in total AI budgets, alongside public filings and third-party reports, according to Menlo.

Unlike closed systems, open-weight models allow developers to download and adapt the underlying parameters rather than access them exclusively via hosted cloud services. Menlo groups such open-weight architectures under the broad label of “open-source”.

Despite the growing adoption of open Chinese architectures, proprietary systems still captured an overwhelming majority of model budgets.

US firms Anthropic and OpenAI commanded a combined 86 per cent of enterprise spending on AI models that were accessed via application programming interfaces (APIs), capturing 55 per cent and 31 per cent respectively, while Google held 9 per cent, the report showed.

In contrast, open-source models represented just 4 per cent of expenditure, even though they accounted for 19 per cent of enterprise usage of tokens – the processing units of AI data.

On global AI model aggregation platform OpenRouter, Chinese models’ token usage exceeded that of US models for the 27th consecutive week from October 26 to November 1.

The dynamic underscores an emerging division across the global AI supply chain: US giants lead in monetising closed-source APIs, while Chinese open models serve as foundations upon which overseas developers adapt to build their own services.

One example is US-based AI coding platform Cursor. In a technical report published in March, Cursor disclosed that its Composer 2 model was built on Moonshot’s Kimi K2.5. The US company refined the Chinese model on code-heavy data sets before applying reinforcement learning to improve its performance in software engineering.

In the report, Menlo said that coding tools and enterprise chatbots now made up 76 per cent of the US$77.3 billion global enterprise AI application market, with autonomous agents driving the next phase of business demand.

Menlo is an active investor in Anthropic, as well as several AI infrastructure providers examined in the report.

Advertisement

Minxiao is a technology reporter at the South China Morning Post, covering semiconductors, AI, and fintech. She previously reported for 36Kr and Harvard Business Review China, specializing in the intersection of AI and emerging technologies. Her coverage focuses on global supply chains, Web3, and RWA.

# Z.ai's GLM-5.5 Surfaces in Leaks and a Tsinghua Lecture — but the Model Still Isn't Released

Details of Z.ai's next flagship, GLM-5.5, leaked through post-training trackers and a lecture by co-founder Jie Tang describing its in-house data pipeline. As of early November 2026 there is still no model card, weights, API, or price.

2026-11-06 · by Moe Ameen

## What happened

Over the first week of November 2026, concrete details about Z.ai's next flagship language model — widely referred to as GLM-5.5 — began circulating, even though Z.ai (the Chinese lab formerly known as Zhipu AI) has not officially announced it. Independent trackers reported the model was deep in post-training by late October, and on November 4 coverage surfaced of a lecture at Tsinghua University by Jie Tang — a Z.ai co-founder and Tsinghua professor — that described the pretraining pipeline behind an upcoming GLM model. The account that drew the most attention came from the AI-watcher @bebuu_ai, which summarized the lecture's claims.

As described, Z.ai is building its pretraining data in-house at very large scale, with a set of internal data engines spanning web pages, documents, books, code, video, and audio. One figure that circulated put the crawled web corpus at on the order of a trillion pages. Separately, internal checkpoint sizes of 32B, 122B, and 256B parameters have been referenced; some observers read these as standalone models, while others argue they are components intended to be merged into a larger system rumored to exceed a trillion total parameters. A "GLM-5.5 Flash" listing has also surfaced on at least one developer platform, though reported as a placeholder with unknown specs — at most a hint Z.ai could repeat the flash/non-flash split it used for GLM-5.3, not a confirmed variant lineup.

None of this is confirmed by Z.ai. As of early November 2026 the company's release notes, pricing page, docs, Hugging Face organization, and GitHub stop at the GLM-5.3 family: GLM-5.3 (the current flagship, released in August 2026) and the cheaper, natively multimodal GLM-5.3-Flash. For reference, Z.ai's officially disclosed lineage showed GLM-5 scaling from GLM-4.5's 355B parameters (32B active) to 744B (40B active), with pretraining data growing from 23 trillion to 28.5 trillion tokens — useful context, but not a spec for 5.5. Treat every GLM-5.5 number — parameter count, context window, open-weight license, and release date — as a leak or an extrapolation until Z.ai publishes a model card.

## Why it matters for creators

- The frontier-model drafting layer keeps getting cheaper and more open. Each GLM release has shipped strong coding and reasoning at a fraction of Western-flagship prices, with MIT-licensed weights — and GLM-5.5 is expected to continue that, which keeps pushing the cost of raw text generation toward the floor.
- For creators, that commoditizes the part of the workflow a raw model touches — drafting scripts and copy — and leaves the real work (visuals, brand identity, and distribution) untouched. A cheaper, stronger model does not get you a published post.
- Nothing is usable yet. You cannot build on GLM-5.5 today; there is no API or weight to call. The actionable move is to use its shipping predecessors now and let the newer model slot in later.
- A cheap, fast tier is a reasonable bet regardless — GLM-5.3 shipped with a low-cost Flash sibling, and a repeat of that split would be good news for anyone who over-generates drafts and wants to spend effort downstream instead.
- Vendor and leak numbers, no third-party audit. GLM benchmark and spec claims have historically been Z.ai's own at launch; a model that is not even out has no verified figures at all.

## How to act on this with Kompozy

The useful way to read a pre-release model is as a cost signal, not a product you can act on. GLM-5.5 is not callable yet, so there is nothing to build on today — but you do not need it to start, because its shipping predecessors already do the drafting job, and the model layer is the interchangeable part of a content operation anyway. The part that does not get cheaper when a new model drops is everything after the draft: on-brand video, images, carousels, a blog, a newsletter, and getting them scheduled and live across every platform. That is the layer [Kompozy](/) owns, and it is indifferent to which model wrote the first draft.

So act on this now. Point today's cheap, open GLM models — [GLM-5.3](/ai-tools/glm-5-3) or the natively multimodal [GLM-5.3-Flash](/ai-tools/glm-5-3-flash) — at your source material and let them draft a batch, then drop the strongest into Kompozy as a source. From that single input Kompozy generates roughly 25–35 finished assets across 18 formats: a captioned [Persona Short](/glossary/persona-shorts) with a face-locked HeyGen avatar, brand-exact [carousels](/glossary/hyperframes), quote graphics, photo posts, a blog article, and an email newsletter — each rewritten under a [Persona Brief](/glossary/persona-brief) so the voice stays yours, then run through a per-post review gate and published by [Autopilot](/glossary/autopilot) across the eight social platforms plus blog and email. When GLM-5.5 actually ships, it changes nothing about this pipeline except which key you point at the drafting step — on the Founding tier you bring your own provider key, so a newer, cheaper model simply becomes your low-cost front end inside the engine.

## Quick takeaways

- GLM-5.5 is unreleased as of early November 2026 — no model card, weights, API, or price from Z.ai.
- Leaks and a Tsinghua lecture by co-founder Jie Tang describe an in-house data pipeline across web, docs, books, code, video, and audio.
- Checkpoint sizes of 32B/122B/256B and a rumored 1T+-parameter system are circulating — all unconfirmed.
- Z.ai's current shipping flagship remains GLM-5.3, with GLM-5.3-Flash as the cheaper multimodal tier.

## Frequently asked questions

### Has GLM-5.5 been released?

Not as of early November 2026. Z.ai has published no model card, weights, API, or pricing for a model called GLM-5.5. Details circulating come from post-training trackers and a reported Tsinghua University lecture by co-founder Jie Tang, not from an official announcement. The current shipping flagship is GLM-5.3, alongside GLM-5.3-Flash.

### What are GLM-5.5's specs?

Unconfirmed. Leaks reference internal checkpoint sizes of 32B, 122B, and 256B parameters and a rumored system exceeding a trillion total parameters, with a context window expected to carry over the GLM family's large window. Z.ai has not stated any of these, so treat every figure as a leak or extrapolation until a model card ships.

### Will GLM-5.5 have open weights?

Likely, based on precedent — GLM-5, GLM-5.2, and GLM-5.3 all published MIT-licensed open weights on Hugging Face — but Z.ai has not confirmed it for GLM-5.5.

### Can I use GLM-5.5 to make social content right now?

No — it is not callable yet, and even once it ships, GLM models output text and code only, not video, images, carousels, or published posts. To turn a GLM draft into finished, on-brand content across platforms you pair it with a generation-and-publishing engine like Kompozy, which can bring your own GLM key in on the Founding tier.

# GLM-5.5

Z.ai's anticipated next flagship language model. As of November 2026 it is unreleased — in post-training, with specs known only from leaks and a lecture by co-founder Jie Tang. The shipping flagship remains GLM-5.3.

Last verified · 2026-11-06 · by Moe Ameen

## What GLM-5.5 is

GLM-5.5 is the next flagship language model expected from Z.ai — the Chinese lab formerly known as Zhipu AI — and, as of early November 2026, it is not released. There is no official model card, no published weights, no API endpoint, and no pricing. What exists is a trail of leaks: independent trackers reported the model was deep in post-training by late October, and in early November coverage surfaced of a lecture at Tsinghua University by Jie Tang, a Z.ai co-founder and Tsinghua professor, describing the pretraining pipeline behind an upcoming GLM model.

The reported details, which Z.ai has not confirmed, describe an in-house data operation: a set of internal data engines building pretraining data across web pages, documents, books, code, video, and audio at very large scale, with one circulated figure putting the crawled web corpus on the order of a trillion pages. Internal checkpoint sizes of 32B, 122B, and 256B parameters have been referenced; observers disagree on whether those are standalone models or components to be merged into a larger system rumored to exceed a trillion total parameters. A "GLM-5.5 Flash" listing has also surfaced on at least one developer platform, though reported as a placeholder with unknown specs and no confirmed launch — at most a hint Z.ai could repeat the flash/non-flash split it used for GLM-5.3, not a confirmed variant lineup.

Context helps calibrate those rumors. Z.ai's officially disclosed lineage showed GLM-5 scaling from GLM-4.5's 355B parameters (32B active) to 744B (40B active), with pretraining data growing from 23 trillion to 28.5 trillion tokens. The current shipping flagship, [GLM-5.3](/ai-tools/glm-5-3), is a coding-and-agent model built on the GLM-5.2 base with a 1-million-token context; its cheaper sibling, [GLM-5.3-Flash](/ai-tools/glm-5-3-flash), is natively multimodal. Every GLM release so far has published MIT-licensed open weights, so GLM-5.5 is widely expected to do the same — but until a model card lands, treat the parameter count, context window, license, and release date as unverified. What is safe to assume from the family: GLM-5.5 will be a text-and-code model tuned for coding, reasoning, and long-horizon agent work, not a content or media generator.

## What you can make with it

- Long, structured video scripts, outlines, and hooks reasoned over a large brief or transcript — if GLM-5.5 carries the family's large context window, a whole content archive fits in one pass
- A batch content plan — angles, series arcs, and per-platform variants — drafted from a single strategy document
- Working automation code: scrapers, ingestion scripts, and small tools that feed a content pipeline on a schedule
- Agentic, multi-step task runs (research, refactors, long-horizon coding) a creator-developer can wire into their own stack
- Technical tutorials, documentation, and code-walkthrough copy for a developer-audience channel
- Nothing visual — like every GLM model, GLM-5.5 is expected to output text and code only, no images, video, or audio

## How Kompozy turns GLM-5.5 output into content

The reason to watch GLM-5.5 is not that it will write a better caption — it is that the GLM line keeps getting stronger at the one thing a drafting front end should do well: reason across a very large input and run long, multi-step work. Hand a future GLM-5.5 a full webinar transcript, a quarter of support tickets, or a sprawling strategy doc and it should come back with a coherent slate of angles, scripts, and hooks, and — if you run it as an agent — the automation to keep pulling fresh source material in. That is a genuinely useful top of the funnel. It is also where it stops: no face, no video, no carousel, no schedule, no published post. [Kompozy](/) is built to take exactly that handoff.

The concrete workflow is model-agnostic by design, which is the point. Today you run that reasoning step on [GLM-5.3](/ai-tools/glm-5-3) or [GLM-5.3-Flash](/ai-tools/glm-5-3-flash); when GLM-5.5 ships, you swap the key and nothing else changes. Drop the model's strongest script into Kompozy as a source and it fans that one input into finished assets — a captioned [Persona Short](/glossary/persona-shorts) with a face-locked HeyGen avatar, a brand-exact [Carousel](/glossary/hyperframes), quote graphics, photo posts, a blog article, and an email newsletter — each rewritten under a [Persona Brief](/glossary/persona-brief) so a batch sounds like one brand instead of raw model output. Then [Autopilot](/glossary/autopilot) schedules and publishes the set across the eight social platforms plus blog and email, every asset clearing a per-post review gate first. Because the Founding tier lets you bring your own provider key, a cheaper, more capable GLM-5.5 just becomes a lower-cost drafting engine behind the same finishing-and-distribution layer.

- Pick your drafting model — GLM-5.3 or GLM-5.3-Flash now, GLM-5.5 when it ships — and reason over a long source into a slate of scripts, outlines, and hooks.
- Optionally run the model as an agent to write the ingestion automation that feeds Kompozy new source material on a cadence.
- Drop the strongest script (or the raw source) into Kompozy as a source and choose your formats.
- Fan that one idea into a persona/avatar short, a carousel, quote graphics, photo posts, a blog, and a newsletter — all in one Persona Brief voice with a consistent face.
- Review each asset in the per-post queue, then let Autopilot schedule and publish across the eight social platforms plus blog and email.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is GLM-5.5 available yet?

No. As of early November 2026, Z.ai has not released GLM-5.5 — there is no model card, no weights, no API, and no pricing. Details circulating come from post-training trackers and a reported Tsinghua lecture by co-founder Jie Tang. The shipping flagship is GLM-5.3, with GLM-5.3-Flash as the cheaper multimodal tier.

### What will GLM-5.5's parameters and context window be?

Unconfirmed. Leaks reference internal checkpoints of 32B, 122B, and 256B parameters and a rumored system over a trillion total parameters, with the context window expected to carry over the GLM family's large window. Z.ai has published none of this, so treat every figure as a leak until an official spec lands.

### Will GLM-5.5 generate images or video for social?

Almost certainly not. Every GLM model to date is a text-in, text-out engine tuned for coding, reasoning, and agents — it produces text and code, not images, video, or audio. To turn a GLM script into visual, published content you pair it with a generation-and-publishing engine like Kompozy.

### How do I turn a GLM-5.5 (or GLM-5.3) script into finished, published content?

Draft the script in the GLM model, then bring it into Kompozy as a source. Kompozy generates a full set of formats from that one input — persona/avatar video, carousels, quote graphics, photo posts, a blog, and a newsletter — holds a consistent face and voice across them, and schedules and publishes across the eight social platforms plus blog and email. On the Founding tier you can bring your own GLM key.

## Related tools

- GLM-5.3 — Z.ai's coding and agent model, released August 14, 2026. It reuses the same 743B-parameter base as GLM-5.2 and gets its gains entirely from scaled post-training, with a 1-million-token context and a jump in long-horizon coding and cybersecurity work.
- GLM-5.3-Flash — Z.ai's cheap, fast, natively multimodal model, launched August 26, 2026 — the model previously teased on OpenRouter as the stealth "Ox Alpha." A 320B-parameter MoE (18B active) with a claimed 1M-token context, MIT open weights, and API pricing near a tenth of the flagship.
- DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 — The general-availability build of DeepSeek's flagship model — a 1.6-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts LLM with a 1M-token context, MIT-licensed weights, and API pricing well under Western frontier models.
- Kimi Work — Moonshot AI's local desktop AI agent for knowledge work — it reads your files, drives your browser, schedules jobs, and runs a swarm of up to ~300 sub-agents on macOS and Windows.

# Revolut Moves 2,000 Engineers to Self-Hosted Chinese AI Model

Revolut has moved around 2,000 engineers from Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex to a self-hosted model developed by Chinese AI company Z.ai.

The switch has brought the company’s AI coding costs down to roughly a tenth of their previous level.

David Abitbol, who oversees AI operations and infrastructure at British Fintech, discussed the move at the AI Engineer conference in New York in October. Revolut now uses Z.ai’s GLM 5.3 as its default coding model. It runs on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs and costs the company around $0.30 per million tokens.

Before the switch, some engineers were spending between $1,000 and $10,000 a month on commercial AI tools. Revolut responded by setting strict limits on token usage. Developers had to be selective about when they used the more expensive models, often saving them for complex coding tasks rather than routine work.

The self-hosted model changed that. With costs no longer tied to individual usage in the same way, Revolut removed the limits. Engineers began using AI for everyday tasks too, including sorting through Jira tickets, searching Confluence and handling email.

Abitbol said the change helped improve coding time by around 60%. Lead time, the period between an engineer picking up a task and getting it ready for deployment, fell by roughly 70%. He attributed much of the improvement to engineers being able to use AI more typically, rather than to a major difference in the model’s coding abilities.

Using a Chinese-developed model in a regulated European financial business has raised some questions. Abitbol acknowledged that Chinese AI models still carry a stigma in this environment. Revolut’s approach is to download the publicly available model weights and run the model on U.S. infrastructure, so data is not sent to servers in China.

The company also keeps engineers involved in the process. AI tools assist with development, but people remain responsible for reviewing and managing the work.

Claude Code and Codex are still available when engineers need them. However, GLM 5.3 is now the default for day-to-day work. Revolut began self-hosting earlier versions of the model in April before moving to the current release.

# Revolut Cut Its AI Coding Bill by 90% by Making Self-Hosted GLM the Default Over Claude Code. What Bootstrapped Founders Can Copy Without 56 GPUs

                                     TL;DR: What did Revolut do with its AI coding tools?

Revolut made a self-hosted open-weight model, Z.ai's GLM, the default AI coding model for its engineers, and kept Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex only "as exception". Its AI operations lead, David Abitbol, said the company serves GLM-5.3 on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs for a sample of about 2,000 engineers, at a blended cost of 30 cents per million tokens, and that "our invoice is one-tenth of what we were spending on Anthropic and OpenAI". The Register reported it on 3 November 2026. You don't need 56 GPUs to use the lesson: rationed tokens cost you more than tokens do, and open models are now good enough for most daily coding work.

If you pay for Claude Code or Codex, you know the feeling. You save your tokens for the hard bug and do the boring work yourself. Revolut, which Abitbol calls Europe's largest private company, had the same problem at a much larger scale, and it decided to stop paying per token.

Its answer was to run a Chinese open-weight model on GPUs it controls and make the frontier models the exception. Here's what Revolut actually did, which numbers you can trust, what it costs you to copy it on a startup budget, and where the risks are.

## What happened

On 13 October 2026, David Abitbol, who leads AI operations at Revolut, gave a short talk called "Shipping like a startup, regulated like a bank" at the AI Engineer conference in New York. On 3 November, The Register reported that Revolut had cut "its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude." The story then spread on Hacker News and LinkedIn.

The key facts from the talk and the article:

- The model. Revolut started with GLM-5.1 and moved to GLM-5.3, both open-weight models from the Chinese lab Z.ai. It serves GLM-5.3 on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. "To serve 2,000 engineers, we roughly need 56 B200," Abitbol said.
- The cost. "Self-hosting GLM, our blended cost of token is 30 cents per million. And so our invoice is one-tenth of what we were spending on Anthropic and OpenAI."
- The tools. Engineers reach the model through OpenAI-compatible endpoints, from tools such as OpenCode and the Codex app, according to the talk.
- The frontier stays. "We keep using Codex, Claude Code," Abitbol said, "but we keep them as exception." GLM is text-only, so a router sends image work to models like Gemini or GPT Luna, The Register reported.

Status: this is Revolut's own account from one conference talk. Revolut hasn't published a blog post or a separate company statement, and all numbers are self-reported.

## Why Revolut switched: rationed tokens were the real cost

The interesting part isn't the GPUs. It's why Revolut started looking. Revolut first brought in Gemini in January 2025 and launched Claude Code at scale in January 2026, Abitbol said in the talk. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said.

Those limits changed how people worked. Engineers saved their tokens for the hardest coding tasks. Once tokens were cheap, they used AI for the work around the code, and that's where Abitbol says the biggest gains came from: debugging, Jira tickets and Confluence pages. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task."

Revolut reports a 60% improvement in coding time and a 70% improvement in lead time across its AI coding rollout. Treat those numbers with care: the conference's own talk page notes that the internal comparison "does not isolate the model change from other causes."

This is the same squeeze we described in our analysis of why AI token bills keep rising: prices per token fall, but agent workloads grow faster. Revolut's fix was to swap a variable bill for a fixed one. In Abitbol's words: "The billing is flat, we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month, and the frontier is the exception."

Revolut's numbers | Value | What to keep in mind 
---|---|---
Engineers in the sample | About 2,000 | Measured over the last year 
GPUs | 56 Nvidia B200 | Owned or rented: not disclosed 
Blended cost | $0.30 per million tokens | Input and output together, Revolut's own calculation 
Bill vs before | One-tenth of Anthropic and OpenAI spend | Staff and hardware costs not broken out 
Coding time, lead time | 60% and 70% better | Not isolated from other changes 
Tuning on the same GPUs | 76% more requests per second, time to first token 14.26 s to 1.68 s | Slide shown in the talk 
Speed engineers accept | Under 3 s to first token, about 200 tokens per second | Complaints start above 5 s 

Sources: David Abitbol's talk at AI Engineer NYC (13 October 2026) and The Register (3 November 2026).

## Why 30 cents isn't the price you'll pay

Be careful with the headline number. The $0.30 is Revolut's blended internal cost per million tokens: what its own GPUs cost divided by the tokens its 2,000 engineers push through them. It's not a price anyone sells, and it's not split into input and output like the vendors' list prices.

Here's what the public API prices look like. On Z.ai's pricing page, GLM-5.3 costs $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens. Anthropic's pricing lists Claude Opus 5.5 at $4 and $20, and Sonnet 5.5 at $2 and $10. OpenAI's pricing lists GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 and $10, GPT-6.1 Terra at $1 and $5, and GPT-5.3 Codex at $1.75 and $14.

Model | Input per 1M tokens | Output per 1M tokens | Weights 
---|---|---|---
GLM-5.3 (Z.ai API) | $1.40 | $4.40 | Open, GLM-5.3 License 
GLM-5.3-Flash (Z.ai API) | $0.15 | $0.50 | Open 
GPT-6.1 Terra | $1.00 | $5.00 | Closed 
Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $2.00 | $10.00 | Closed 
GPT-6.1 Sol | $2.00 | $10.00 | Closed 
GPT-5.3 Codex | $1.75 | $14.00 | Closed 
Claude Opus 5.5 | $4.00 | $20.00 | Closed 
Revolut, self-hosted GLM | $0.30 blended | $0.30 blended | Its own deployment 

Sources: official pricing pages of Z.ai, Anthropic and OpenAI, read 6 November 2026; Revolut's figure from the AI Engineer NYC talk. Standard prices, before caching and batch discounts.

So a small team can't get 30 cents. What it can get is a hosted open model that's several times cheaper per output token than the top closed models, with no GPUs to run. The 30 cents only shows up at Revolut's scale, where 56 GPUs stay busy all day. A 56-GPU cluster sitting idle for a five-person startup would cost far more than any subscription.

## What you need to know about GLM

GLM-5.1 went up on Hugging Face on 3 April 2026 under the plain MIT licence, with about 754 billion parameters, according to its model card. The Register reports that only about 40 billion are active for each token, and that the weights alone need roughly 380 GB of GPU memory. GLM-5.3 followed on 25 August 2026, with a one-million-token context window.

The licence changed with 5.3. The GLM-5.3 License is MIT-style, but adds one condition: if a company runs a "Model as a Service" business and its group revenue tops $10 billion over any 12 months, it "must pass Z.AI's security review before using the Software or its derivative works for any commercial purpose." That won't touch a bootstrapped startup. It's still a reminder to read the licence of every open model you build on, because they change between versions, as Mistral's did with Large 4.

Two tuning lessons from the talk apply to anyone running a model. First, "Long context is a scam," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need." Second, Revolut got its biggest gains by tuning the GPUs it already had, with NVFP4 quantization and split prefill and decode, not by buying more.

## The China question

GLM comes from a Chinese lab, and Revolut is a regulated bank. Abitbol's view, as The Register reports it, is that the main privacy and security worry is using Chinese models through APIs running out of China. When the weights run on-premises or on regional cloud servers, he says, there's really nothing to worry about. "You're just getting the weights and putting them on a US-based service," he said in the talk.

He also described the controls that make this acceptable to a regulator: "because we're an EU-regulated bank, we fall under the most strict regime in terms of compliance." Agents run in sandboxes with tight command rules, for example "allow grep but not gradle". That, he said, gives "confidence to your regulator that it's not an autonomous agent". The talk page notes these comments describe Revolut's own situation, not general legal advice.

Not everyone is convinced. Hirundo, a company that sells AI safety tools, published its own test on 3 November using GLM-5.3-Flash through OpenRouter, not Revolut's setup. It reported that account-recovery code was 28% more likely to be open to takeover when the repository named Revolut than when it named WeBank, a Chinese digital bank. That's a vendor's study, not peer-reviewed, but it's a good reason to keep code review strict whatever model writes the code.

There's also a supply risk. China has drafted export controls on its biggest AI models, as we covered in our post on China's AI export rules. Published open weights are exempt in that draft, but rules can change. And in October, Cohere said Alibaba's Qwen model tried to upload a file to a Beijing cloud bucket during an agent test, which we wrote up in our post on the Qwen upload incident. Self-hosting doesn't remove the need for a sandbox.

Kimi.content:
## Kimi发布托管智能体服务：7×24小时运行，内置140多项Skills

11月5日，月之暗面（Moonshot AI）宣布推出 Kimi Hosted Agents（托管智能体） 服务，将支撑AI智能体（Agent）运行的Harness框架作为云端服务提供给企业和开发者。企业无需自行搭建和维护底层运行框架，即可获得7×24小时托管运行环境，支持长时间复杂任务执行及多智能体协作。

据介绍，Kimi Hosted Agents主要面向两类应用场景：一是集成到企业内部系统，承担业务监控、运维响应等工作；二是嵌入企业面向用户的产品，提供投研助手、智能客服等服务。

在传统开发模式下，企业要让AI智能体稳定运行，通常需要自行搭建代码执行环境，并解决上下文管理、工具调用、权限控制、任务中断恢复等问题。Kimi表示，企业构建一套可靠的Harness基础设施可能需要数月时间，后续还需持续投入维护成本。

Kimi Hosted Agents将上述能力封装为托管服务，企业只需定义任务、配置智能体并接入业务工具，底层运行环境的维护和升级由Kimi负责，以缩短AI智能体从原型开发到实际部署的周期。

在工具生态方面，Kimi Hosted Agents提供140多项Skills（技能）和30多个插件，覆盖联网检索、专业数据查询、办公文档处理、内容生成等场景。开发者既可以调用官方工具，也可以接入企业自有的数据源和业务系统。

安全方面，该平台提供独立沙箱、网络访问权限控制、会话中止和执行审计等功能，企业可以限制智能体的操作范围，并通过用量报表管理资源消耗与成本。

Kimi还介绍了独立安全组件Kimi Inference Hook。该组件可以对接企业自建或采购的安全服务，在每次模型推理前检查任务输入和工具返回内容，由企业制定安全检查规则，决定是否允许相关内容进入模型推理流程。目前，该功能仅面向企业认证用户定向开放。

针对实际业务落地，Kimi首批提供8个金融领域Agent模板，覆盖投研建模、深度研究、金融晨报、IPO跟踪、持仓监控等任务。企业可将模板复制到自己的项目空间，接入内部研报、私有数据库等资源，构建能够在托管环境中持续运行的业务智能体。

Kimi此前已在今年9月推出Hosted Agents Beta版本，提供会话管理、工具执行、沙箱及失败恢复等能力。此次发布进一步展示了平台的工具生态、安全控制与行业应用方案。

Kimi Hosted Agents现已提供开放平台使用入口，开发者可通过控制台、API或命令行工具配置和运行智能体。

# Day-0 支持：摩尔线程完成 3 万亿级参数 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 适配，支持文本与图片推理

2026-11-06 22:41 IT之家 - 归泷

感谢IT之家网友 Autumn_Dream 的线索投递！

IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，本月 4 日，月之暗面正式公布 Kimi K3.1 Pro 完整模型权重。在 Arena 运营的 Agent Arena 智能体排行榜中，Kimi K3.1 Pro（Max）位列开放权重模型第一、全部参评模型第 13 位，并在工作、编程与聊天三个类别中均居开放模型首位。

摩尔线程官方今日宣布，摩尔线程基于 AI 训推一体智算卡 MTT S5000 及 MUSA 软件栈，完成 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 模型的 Day-0 适配，打通模型加载、服务启动及文本、图片基础推理链路。

IT之家了解到，Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 K3.1 系列首款模型，也是迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。经过大规模后训练和强化学习，模型在代码、3D 创作、金融研究、知识问答及长程 Agent 任务等方面均全面提升；在代码与 Agent 基准测试中，其表现已达到或接近顶尖闭源模型水平：Terminal-Bench 4.0 得分 65.7%，Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。

摩尔线程官方表示，围绕 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的模型架构与计算特性，其通过 MUSA 软件栈，完成了关键推理路径迁移与适配，支持模型在 MTT S5000 上稳定运行。

MUSA 软件栈高兼容，支撑新模型快速迁移：MUSA 在编程模型、运行时接口和 AI 框架层面的快速兼容迁移能力，是本次快速适配的重要基础。团队基于 SGLang-MUSA 承接上游模型实现，并通过 MATE 算子库、Triton-MUSA、TileLang-MUSA 及 MTCC 编译器，完成新架构关键计算路径的迁移与接入，将社区模型代码转化为 MTT S5000 上的实际推理服务。MUSA 软件栈同时覆盖框架执行、算子编译、设备运行和多卡通信，使模型适配能够复用成熟接口，并针对新增计算路径开展优化。

接入 DSA，打通混合注意力与视觉计算：针对 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 的稀疏注意力 DSA，MUSA 软件栈完成索引选择、KV 缓存布局及 Prefill、Decode 计算路径的适配，接入 MATE 稀疏注意力算子，并与 KDA 状态管理、跨层残差及视觉 Attention 共同组成完整执行链路。面对模型采用的 MXFP4 专家权重，团队通过在线转换与跨层复用 FP8 工作区的方式执行专家计算，无需预先生成完整的离线 FP8 权重，为超大模型快速部署提供支持。

Kimi.content:
互联网

# Kimi K3.1 Pro 全量权重 11 月 4 日前开源：2.8 万亿参数、100 万上下文，开源后将成为 AA 智能指数最高开源模型

导语：月之暗面发布 Kimi K3.1 Pro，是 K3.1 系列首款模型，也是其迄今能力最强的 3T 级开放权重模型，上下文窗口 100 万 token。

### 摘要：

月之暗面发布 Kimi K3.1 Pro，是 K3.1 系列首款模型，也是其迄今能力最强的 3T 级开放权重模型，上下文窗口 100 万 token。它在编程、3D 创作、金融研究和长程智能体任务上有显著提升，官方承诺完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前开源。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 评测中得分 65.7%，超过 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅差不到 1 个百分点。同步推出 Highspeed 版本，输出速度是标准版的 2 至 3 倍。官方刻意压低了开源版本的攻击性网络能力，安全能力按阶段渐进释放。

### 正文（译文）：

我们推出 Kimi K3.1 Pro，这是 K3.1 系列的首款模型，也是我们迄今能力最强的 3T 级开放权重模型，上下文窗口为 100 万 token。它在编程、3D 创作、金融研究以及其他智能体能力上带来显著提升。

我们同时发布 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed，其响应速度是 K3.1 Pro 的 2 至 3 倍。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 与 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 今日起已在 Kimi.ai、Kimi Work、Kimi Code 和 Kimi API 上线。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Kimi K3 的后训练版本，后训练算力大幅增加。为在数百个下游领域开展大规模联合强化学习，我们优化了技术栈的每一层，包括强化学习框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、调度系统，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台，确保每一份新增的强化学习算力都能转化为稳定、可预期的回报。最终，K3.1 Pro 在所有领域都取得了稳定的提升。

在编程、智能体和知识类基准上，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强的闭源模型。在考察编程智能体在真实、资源受限的终端任务上表现的 Terminal-Bench 4.0 中，K3.1 Pro 得分 65.7%，领先 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅差不到 1 个百分点。在我们内部的 Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 基准上，K3.1 Pro 得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。

开放权重原则。这些评估框定了我们开源权重的决策。首先，我们无意发布会扩大网络攻击绝对前沿能力的开放权重。K3.1 Pro 的攻击性网络能力经过设计，低于我们技术栈所能达到的水平，也仍落后于前沿闭源模型。其次，我们计划逐步提升开放权重中的网络能力。我们相信，以非歧视的方式开放 K3.1 Pro，能让出于防御目的需要双重用途能力的人受益。当一个能力较强的模型开放、并运行在用户自己掌控的基础设施上时，更多团队就有能力审计他们维护的代码，包括那些很少得到专门安全审查的遗留系统。让这种能力渐进扩散，而不是集中在少数闭源系统中，最终会让所有软件都更安全。

（文章为作者独立观点，不代表艾瑞网立场）

IT之家了解到，Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 K3.1 系列首款模型，也是迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。经过大规模后训练和强化学习，模型在代码、3D 创作、金融研究、知识问答及长程 Agent 任务等方面均全面提升；在代码与 Agent 基准测试中，其表现已达到或接近顶尖闭源模型水平：Terminal-Bench 4.0 得分 65.7%，Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。

摩尔线程官方表示，围绕 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的模型架构与计算特性，其通过 MUSA 软件栈，完成了关键推理路径迁移与适配，支持模型在 MTT S5000 上稳定运行。

MUSA 软件栈高兼容，支撑新模型快速迁移：MUSA 在编程模型、运行时接口和 AI 框架层面的快速兼容迁移能力，是本次快速适配的重要基础。团队基于 SGLang-MUSA 承接上游模型实现，并通过 MATE 算子库、Triton-MUSA、TileLang-MUSA 及 MTCC 编译器，完成新架构关键计算路径的迁移与接入，将社区模型代码转化为 MTT S5000 上的实际推理服务。MUSA 软件栈同时覆盖框架执行、算子编译、设备运行和多卡通信，使模型适配能够复用成熟接口，并针对新增计算路径开展优化。

接入 DSA，打通混合注意力与视觉计算：针对 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 的稀疏注意力 DSA，MUSA 软件栈完成索引选择、KV 缓存布局及 Prefill、Decode 计算路径的适配，接入 MATE 稀疏注意力算子，并与 KDA 状态管理、跨层残差及视觉 Attention 共同组成完整执行链路。面对模型采用的 MXFP4 专家权重，团队通过在线转换与跨层复用 FP8 工作区的方式执行专家计算，无需预先生成完整的离线 FP8 权重，为超大模型快速部署提供支持。

xAI.content:
# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

- xai:grok-4.5 - Flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)
- xai:grok-4.5-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family
- xai:grok-build-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family

### Grok 4.3 Models

- xai:grok-4.3 - General-purpose reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.3-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family
- xai:grok-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family

### Grok 4.20 Models

- xai:grok-4.20-0309-reasoning - Reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.20 - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning - Non-reasoning variant
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 - Multi-agent variant
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family

### Grok 4.1 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok Code Fast Models

- xai:grok-build-0.1 - Canonical Grok Build coding model (256K context)
- xai:grok-code-fast-1 - Legacy alias that routes to grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast - Alias for grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast-1-0825 - Versioned alias for grok-build-0.1

### Grok-4 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-fast-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-fast-non-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok-4 Models

- xai:grok-4-0709, xai:grok-4, and xai:grok-4-latest - Legacy IDs that redirect to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort

### Grok-3 Models

Thegrok-3, grok-3-beta, grok-3-fast, and related -latest IDs are legacy aliases that redirect to Grok 4.3. Promptfoo also recognizes the older Grok 3 Mini IDs for backward compatibility; verify their availability for your xAI account before relying on them.

### Grok-2 and previous Models

Promptfoo recognizes oldergrok-2, grok-beta, and vision IDs for existing configs, but they are not in xAI's current public catalog. Use a current model for new configs and verify legacy availability in the xAI Console.

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI-compatible configuration options plus Grok-specific options, subject to the model restrictions below. Example usage:

When xAI returnsusage.cost_in_usd_ticks, Promptfoo uses that exact billed amount, including cache discounts and request-level pricing adjustments. If ticks are unavailable, Promptfoo falls back to the model's catalog rates and applies the documented 2x premium when the response confirms service_tier: priority. Custom pricing can be set with cost, inputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost (all per-token rates); explicit overrides take precedence over reported ticks and are used as final rates without an additional priority multiplier.
providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.7
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: 'xhigh' # low, medium, high (default), or xhigh
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to XAI_API_KEY

Bothxai:<model> Chat Completions and xai:responses:<model> support xAI
Priority Processing.
Set service_tier to priority for higher scheduling priority or default for standard
processing; omitting it also uses the default tier. Other OpenAI-compatible tier names are not
valid on xAI.

### Reasoning Support

Multiple Grok models support reasoning capabilities:

Grok 4.7 and 4.6: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, high (the default), or xhigh. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort. Reasoning cannot be disabled; Promptfoo rejects none locally.

For Grok 4.7, cap output withmax_completion_tokens for Chat Completions or max_output_tokens for Responses. Chat also accepts max_tokens as an alias; use one spelling throughout an eval, including defaults and test cases. Within test options, set a request option directly or under passthrough, not both. Reasoning effort accepts a direct eval variable such as {{ effort }}; see the optional Grok 4.7 providers in the xAI chat example.

Grok 4.5: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, or high (the default); Promptfoo rejects other values locally. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort with the same values.

Grok 4.3: General-purpose reasoning model. Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high; Responses API requests use reasoning.effort.

Grok Code Fast Models: Thegrok-code-fast-1 family are reasoning models optimized for agentic coding workflows. They support:

- Function calling and tool usage
- Web search viasearch_parameters
- Fast inference with built-in reasoning

### Grok 4.7 Specific Behavior

The xAI release notes list $2/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $6/M output. At 200K or more input tokens, the rates are $4/M, $1/M, and $12/M respectively. When the API does not return a billed cost, Promptfoo uses these rates, including the 10% premium on xAI's US endpoint; explicit custom rates still take precedence. As with other Grok 4 reasoning models, Promptfoo stripspresence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop.

The Responses API returns encrypted reasoning even wheninclude is omitted. Promptfoo keeps it in response.raw.output; pass these items back unchanged when managing conversation history yourself.

### Grok 4.5 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.5 is an earlier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work:

- 500K context window with text and image input
- Configurable reasoning:reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, or high (defaults to high); none is rejected
- Long-context pricing: requests with at least 200K input tokens use the higher catalog rate ($4/M input, $0.60/M cached input, and $12/M output instead of $2/M, $0.30/M, and $6/M); Promptfoo uses the exact billed ticks when xAI returns them
- Unsupported parameters:presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop are rejected, and Promptfoo strips them automatically
- Ignored parameters: xAI silently ignoreslogprobs and top_logprobs on Grok 4.20 and newer models
- Server-side tools: usexai:responses:grok-4.5 for web search, X search, code execution, and MCP

providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.5
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: medium
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

### Grok 4.3 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.3 is a general-purpose alternative for text workflows:

- Responses API recommended: Usexai:responses:grok-4.3 for server-side tools, multi-turn state, and newer xAI capabilities
- Configurable reasoning: Setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high
- Unsupported parameters: Same restrictions as other Grok 4-family reasoning models (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop)

providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.3
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      max_completion_tokens: 4096

Grok-3 Models: Promptfoo retains the legacy Grok 3 Mini reasoning-effort contract for backward compatibility. Use Grok 4.3 or Grok 4.7 for new configurations.

### Grok 4.1 Fast Specific Behavior

These retired IDs redirect to Grok 4.3 but retain their legacy request contract. Promptfoo stripsreasoning_effort, presence_penalty, freque

# Coforge joins SpaceX Super Intelligence partner network to take Grok into enterprise production

Through its specialized unit, Momentuum blue, Coforge will integrate Grok technology within client infrastructures. This collaboration aims to blend Coforge's engineering prowess with SpaceXSI's innovative capabilities to ensure tangible business advantages through AI-driven solutions.

PRINCETON, N.J. and GREATER NOIDA, India — November 6, 2026 — Coforge today announced that it has joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI) Partner Network as a Transformation Partner. Coforge will help enterprises put the Grok portfolio to work in their business workflows, building solutions grounded in each client’s operating context and taking them into production with measurable business value.
Coforge will take Grok into production through Momentuum blue, its specialized Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) operating unit. Momentuum blue operates within client environments, embedding pods of senior FDEs, associate FDEs, and AI agents that have full accountability for delivering business outcomes measured against an agreed baseline.

“Our opportunity with SpaceXSI is to help clients put the Grok portfolio to work across their businesses,” said Anup Nair, Executive Vice President and Chief AI Commercial Officer, Coforge.

“From software modernization and customer service to enterprise applications, we bring the industry context, engineering expertise and adoption capabilities to turn Grok’s technology into solutions that are grounded in how each client actually operates."

The Grok portfolio includes Grok for chat, research, and analysis; Grok Models for reasoning; Grok Build for software development; Grok Bot for ongoing work across enterprise applications; Grok Voice for conversational experiences; and Grok Imagine for image and video creation. The Grok API provides a route to integrate these capabilities into enterprise solutions.

“Coforge pairs deep engineering and industry experience with a delivery model built to get Grok running in production, inside the systems clients depend on every day,” said Toni Adams, Head of Global Partnerships, SpaceXSI. “We’re glad to have Coforge in the network and look forward to working together to help our joint customers get measurable results from Grok.”

The SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network is SpaceXSI’s official program for companies building products, solutions, and services with Grok for joint prospects and customers. Transformation Partners help customers deploy the Grok platform across the enterprise and create tangible business value.

# Coforge partners with SpaceX to deploy Grok across enterprise workflows

0 0

Coforge has joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network as a Transformation Partner, with plans to help enterprises deploy Grok across business workflows and applications.

The partnership will focus on taking Grok-based solutions from development to production, integrating them with existing enterprise systems and adapting them to organisations’ operational requirements. Coforge will use its Momentuum blue unit, which specialises in Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), to support these deployments.

Forward Deployed Engineering to support enterprise deployment

Coforge said Momentuum blue will work within client environments through teams comprising senior and associate FDEs, alongside AI agents. These teams will be responsible for delivering outcomes against performance baselines agreed with clients.

The FDE model involves embedding engineering teams within an organisation to understand its business processes and build solutions around its specific requirements. In this partnership, the approach is intended to help enterprises integrate Grok into their existing applications and workflows rather than use it as a standalone AI tool.

Coforge will also draw on its AI-led engineering and modernisation services, along with Nuuron, its enterprise AI enablement suite, and its industry-specific expertise.

Grok capabilities for enterprise applications

The Grok portfolio includes models and tools for research, reasoning, software development, enterprise application workflows, voice-based interactions, and image and video generation. The Grok API can also be used to integrate these capabilities into enterprise solutions.

According to Coforge, potential areas of deployment include software modernisation, customer service and enterprise applications. The company plans to adapt these capabilities to the systems and operating environments of individual clients.

Anup Nair, Executive Vice President and Chief AI Commercial Officer at Coforge, said the partnership would combine Grok’s capabilities with the company’s engineering expertise and industry knowledge to develop solutions suited to client operations.

Focus on moving AI from pilots to production

The partnership reflects the growing focus among enterprises on integrating generative AI into business processes and operational systems. While organisations have been experimenting with AI tools across functions, deploying them at scale requires integration with existing applications, workflows and enterprise data.

The SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network is a programme for companies developing products, solutions and services using Grok. As a Transformation Partner, Coforge will work with SpaceX to support enterprise deployments for joint customers.
