商汤科技开源的模型

# SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview

SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview是商汤科技于2026年10月30日开源的模型。 [1]

该模型采用Looped Transformer架构，引入循环计算、扩展模型的有效计算深度，并探索信息交互机制，旨在提升模型在复杂任务上的处理能力 [1]。该模型参数规模为9B [3]。模型以9B尺度模型为基座，将中间层改造为参数共享的循环计算模块，通过多轮迭代扩展有效计算深度，并尝试引入mHC [1]。

中文名
    商汤日日新

外文名
    SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview

开发公司
    商汤科技

## 目录

  1. 1研发背景
  2. 2发展历程
  3. 3能力与应用

  1. 4核心技术
  2. 5性能表现
  3. 6行业影响

## 研发背景

大模型能力的提升并不只有扩大参数规模一条路径。SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview是商汤面向下一代模型架构的一项探索，整体设计旨在控制参数规模的同时，通过增加有效计算深度来提升模型推理能力 [4]。

此前，围绕Looped Transformer的研究多停留在学术层面，社区缺少可直接面向日常使用的开源模型。此次开源为社区提供了9B级Looped Transformer的开源实践 [4]。

## 发展历程

2026年10月30日，商汤科技宣布开源商汤日日新SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview [5]。北京时间10月30日20时51分，商汤科技官方X账号@SenseTime_AI发布开源公告，模型权重发布于Hugging Face、代码发布于GitHub，采用Apache 2.0许可。GitHub仓库于2026年10月30日更新，技术报告一栏标着TBD，兼容Transformers的官方实现“发布细节待公布” [6]。

## 能力与应用

SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview是支持文本与图像输入、文本输出的多模态模型，训练上下文最长可达262,144 tokens，支持长上下文与智能体工作流等应用场景 [7]。

Hugging Face仓库提供中英双语README，以及动效设计、PPT设计、数据分析三类演示，并包含可交互的动态HTMLdemo [6]。

## 核心技术

SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview采用Looped Transformer架构，通过引入循环计算扩展模型的有效计算深度，并探索更充分的信息交互机制，提升模型在复杂任务上的处理能力 [1]。

模型以9B尺度模型为基座，保留首尾各4层原始解码器模块，将中间层改造为参数共享的循环计算模块，通过多轮迭代扩展有效计算深度。32层解码器中，第4～27层组成的模块以共享权重连续执行两次，加上首尾各4层，模型每次前向传播完成56层计算，但只需存储32层的权重 [6]。

在此基础上，模型进一步探索循环计算中的信息传递机制，尝试引入mHC（Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections），利用多路残差连接与受约束的信息混合，增强特征交互并维持信号传播的稳定性。mHC作用在循环段内：两条残差流并行携带信息，可学习的映射决定每一层从流里读什么、怎么混合、把输出写回哪里，流混合矩阵用Sinkhorn归一化约束，文档配置为20次迭代 [6]。

商汤通过消融实验评估了mHC的实际收益。采用该机制后，模型取得明显性能提升，其中GPQA Diamond和TeamBench分别提高4.42分和13.34分 [1]。

注意力为混合结构：每4层一组，3层线性注意力加1层全注意力，循环边界与完整的4层组对齐，两次循环的注意力模式一致。模型卡列出总参数约9B、“推理参数”约14.6B，隐藏维度4,096、前馈维度12,288、词表248,320、全注意力头16个、KV头4个；权重以BF16导出，mHC路由参数为FP32 [6]。

运行需要Transformers 5.18.0与PyTorch2.11.0/CUDA13.0，并以trust_remote_code加载自定义模型实现；官方给出的部署路径包括LightLLM的四卡容器示例，或SGLang的PR #47281分支 [6]。

## 性能表现

该模型在仅9B参数规模下，在部分评测中与27B参数规模模型表现相当 [8]，在代码生成、办公场景和智能体任务等多个评测方向上均优于对比模型 [2]。

商汤公布的基准图覆盖8个基准，其中6项领先全部对比模型，2项落后于Qwen3.5-27B。具体来看，WorkBuddy Bench为66.89（Qwen3.5-27B为60.53）、RaccoonPPT Bench为70.70（对比59.08）、AutomationBench为13.72（对比10.17）、BIRD-Dev为71.38（对比69.84）、AIDABench为58.87（对比57.19）、TeamBench为48.89（对比44.44）；Terminal Bench 2.1为40.45，低于Qwen3.5-27B的47.19和Nanbeige 4.2-3B的49.44；τ³-Banking为18.56，低于Qwen3.5-27B的19.59 [6]。

以上评测数字均来自商汤自报 [6]。

## 行业影响

相关评测结果初步展现了通过扩展有效计算深度、提升小参数模型复杂任务处理能力的潜力。商汤表示，后续还将继续探索DSA、自适应迭代次数等机制，以进一步提升模型的推理效率与任务表现 [1]。

# Intel offers Day-0 dupport for Meta's Muse Spark open data center silicon built for 816B scale

## Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model. Trained specifically for agentic coding workflows, it delivers higher first-attempt accuracy, reliable tool calling, etc.

New Update

Listen to this article

0.75x1x1.5x

00:00/ 00:00

Meta’s official open-weight release of Muse Spark Open, an 816 billion-parameter any-to-text model, represents a major milestone in multimodal AI and the most capable U.S. open-weights model released to date.

Deploying an 816 billion-parameter architecture requires extreme memory efficiency and hardware-level low-precision acceleration. Intel has enabled day-0 support across Intel Xeon® processors and Intel data center GPU platforms, Intel GPU D-series, through targeted low-bit model quantization.

Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model. Trained specifically for agentic coding workflows, it delivers higher first-attempt accuracy, reliable tool calling, and deep codebase understanding across the repositories developers use.

This open-weight model is strong in code generation, debugging and codebase understanding. The 1 million-token context window handles entire projects, including complex dependencies, legacy code and thousands of files, without requiring tasks to be broken into smaller pieces. Muse Spark Open also supports multimodal understanding, including audio, video, image, and document comprehension.

Advertisment

For agentic use cases, Muse Spark Open was built to plan, act, observe and self-correct over extended workflows. It is trained to browse the web, including multimodal content, use an agentic harness to spawn and coordinate subagents for decomposable work, and leverage computer-use capabilities across desktop, mobile and browser environments.

Data center silicon built for 816 billion-parameter scale
Large language models at the scale of Meta’s Muse Spark Open highlight the growing infrastructure demands of advanced AI workloads. At hundreds of billions of parameters, they require substantial memory capacity, efficient low-precision compute, power efficiency and architectures that can bring these capabilities into existing data center footprints.

Muse Spark Open has been tested and is running on the upcoming Intel GPU D-series, today. This early work reflects Intel’s commitment to day-0 support for emerging AI models and gives customers an early path to begin evaluating Muse Spark Open on Intel silicon.

Muse Spark Open inference was running on four Intel GPU D-series GPUs. Each GPU provides 160 GB of memory, offering sufficient capacity to run Muse Spark Open across four GPUs.

Intel GPU D-series is designed for the demands of large and agentic AI models. Built on the Intel Xe3P architecture, it features:
* 32 Xe3P cores
* 256 Intel XMX engines
* Dedicated hardware acceleration across a broad range of data types, including MXFP4
* 160 GB LPDDR5x memory capacity, with options up to 480 GB.

These capabilities are well aligned with large-model inference, combining low-precision compute with high memory capacity to support models such as Muse Spark Open efficiently. Its 350W air-cooled PCIe form factor also simplifies deployment. A compact four-card configuration can host an 816 billion-parameter-class model within conventional air-cooled data center racks, helping reduce infrastructure complexity for organizations evaluating frontier-scale AI.

Muse Spark Open on Intel Xeon processors
Designed for high-capacity CPU inference, Intel Xeon processors support INT4 weight-only quantized (WOQ) inference, reducing memory footprint, while leveraging Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel AMX) to accelerate AI matrix operations.

Given the size of the model, Intel Xeon processors provide a practical path for offline inference by taking advantage of large system memory capacities, enabling organizations to run workloads privately and replicate deployments across existing Intel Xeon infrastructure in their data centers.

Intel is announcing day-0 support for Muse Spark Open on Xeon processors. For step-by-step instructions on running Muse Spark Open on Xeon processors with SGLang, see the SGLang cookbook. Intel is also working closely with the vLLM community to add Xeon recipes.

Software support and enablement
Intel’s Upstreaming First software strategy helps enterprise AI engineering teams deploy both quantized variants using standard open-source tools.

Full upstream support for compressed tensors, such as MXFP4, and GPTQ (INT4 WOQ) in mainline vLLM enables hardware-accelerated matrix execution, continuous batching and PagedAttention across multinode deployments. Native upstream integration for microscaling (MX) execution and Intel XPU-optimized kernels in SGLang drives high-throughput continuous batching and low-bit inference for complex, multiturn agentic workflows.

To maximize efficiency on Intel silicon without sacrificing accuracy, Intel quantized MXFP4 and INT4 variants directly from Muse Spark Open’s original BF16 weights using vLLM’s native quantization tool, llm-compressor, powered by the AutoRound quantization algorithm.

Intel’s AutoRound algorithm optimizes rounding and clipping-range parameters layer by layer, helping preserve Muse Spark Open’s fine-grained reasoning capabilities even at ultra-low bit widths.

The MXFP4 weights, in compressed-tensors format, target Intel GPU D-series GPUs to use native hardware acceleration, while the INT4 weights, in GPTQ format, support Xeon processors in weight-only quantization mode to minimize memory footprint and latency.

Combining upstream support in vLLM and SGLang with hardware-tailored MXFP4 and INT4 WOQ execution gives enterprise teams the performance and agility needed to run Meta’s 816 billion-parameter Muse Spark Open on day 0.

Summary
Intel Xeon processors offer an alternative approach for offline inference with Meta’s Muse Spark Open 816 billion-parameter model. Additionally, the upcoming Intel data center GPU, Intel GPU D-series, is designed for the demands of large and agentic AI models and provides 160 GB of memory per GPU. A compact four-card configuration can host Muse Spark Open within conventional air-cooled data center racks.

cross_cutting.content:
# Mira Murati 公司第二代模型来了：Inkling 2 Small 首日闭门、下周开源，AA Index 直接冲到 31

TL;DR：11 月 5 日，Thinking Machines Lab（Mira Murati 创立）发布第二代模型 Inkling 2 Small：594B 总参数、17B 激活的 MoE，支持图像输入与可调思考力度。Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 拿下 31 分，远超前代。玩法延续自家「安全开放」路线：今天就能在 Tinker 上用（闭门权重），Apache 2.0 全权重承诺下周外部安全测试完成后放出。训练细节也大方公开：预训练 68 小时跑完 GB300 机架、原生 NVFP4，一次 9 天的联合 RL 完成 1700 万次 rollouts。

资源

## 这次发布的是什么

Thinking Machines Lab 的节奏很稳：7 月发了首个开放权重模型 Inkling，两周后跟上缩小版 Inkling-Small（276B/12B），10 月庆祝 Tinker 一周年，11 月 5 日直接掏出第二代——Inkling 2 Small。

配置单：

- MoE 架构，594B 总参数 / 17B 激活——总参逼近 600B 但每 token 只激活 17B，推理成本控制在「Small」该有的水平；
- 支持图像输入，多模态；
- Variable effort（可调思考力度）——同一个模型，简单问题快答、难题深思，力度由调用方或模型自己定。

成绩上，官方主打的数字是 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 得分 31，官方原话是「far surpasses our previous models」。分项看更有信息量：JobBench 70.5%、Vals Legal Index 73.9%、HLE-Diamond 28.7% 都是开放权重模型里的最高分；AA-Briefcase（端到端知识工作基准）ELO 1527；金融方向 AA-AnalystAgent 和 Dayjob:Finance 开放权重第一——这家公司对「知识工作 + 金融量化」的偏爱一如既往。

## 演示有多能打

官方放了四个 demo，每个都值得展开说：

- 城市模拟器：用 Three.js 从零搭出完整城市游戏，所有建筑、纹理、车辆全部程序化生成，没有一个预制资产——玩家从一条路开始经营整座活的城市，还要管电力、预算和突发事件；
- PC 模拟器：一个 Python 从零写的 PC 模拟器，能启动真正的 Linux 内核，还带 web 界面在浏览器里跑 live 实例；
- Blender 创作视频：手绘风格的纸面山谷，折纸鹤落下来，水波和烟囱的改进是按反馈迭代出来的；
- 户型图漫游：从一张平面图生成可走动的 3D 漫游。

这几个 demo 共同点不是「刷榜分高」，而是长程自主工作：模型要在几十分钟的连续任务里自己规划、执行、看反馈、修正——官方也明说这一代最大的进步就在这里。

## 训练细节：这才是同行最该看的

Thinking Machines 这次把训练栈讲得相当透，信息量远超一般厂商通稿：

预训练四阶段：H1 用 8.4T tokens（自然语言/代码/图像混合）打底，在 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 机架上只跑了 68 小时，靠机架级专家并行把效率拉满，且全程原生 NVFP4（Blackwell 的 4-bit 浮点格式）——NVFP4 配方细节官方说后续文章再讲。H2 换 3.8T 更高质量的新数据、512K 上下文；H3 混入约 320B 推理与 agent 轨迹（1M 上下文）；H4 只留约 34B 最高质量轨迹。注意 H3/H4 的数据大部分是从早期模型（包括 Kimi K3 和自家模型）采样的轨迹、过滤后回炉的——轨迹蒸馏的路数已经很成熟了。

一次联合 RL：1075 步、超过 1700 万次 rollouts、9 天、2048 块 GPU、总算力超过 4×10²³ FLOPs。重点是「一次」——上一代 Inkling 是分开跑 reasoning RL 和 agentic RL 再用多教师蒸馏合并，这一代直接一锅端。任务混合里 Coding 占 38.5%（消耗 65% tokens），办公知识工作 9.1%，视觉 13.9%，工具使用 17.1%。

编码特训的三个巧思：数十万长程编码任务跨多个 agent harness 与上下文压缩策略训练；奖励不只看单元测试过没过，还安排了「agentic RL grader」评模型解题的过程；甚至用早期 checkpoint 化名 Fledge-Alpha 悄悄放到 OpenCode 上做真实环境测试——匿名参赛测真实水平，这个操作挺有意思。

effort 怎么学的：训练时随机采样一个 effort 水平作为条件，奖励函数里加长度惩罚，逼模型学会「速度 vs 彻底性」的权衡。异步 RL 用的是 Tinker 的 StableReinforce 目标，能容忍明显的策略陈旧性；长程任务配 256K 上下文 + compaction 训练，p99 单次 rollout 长达 4 小时、1.5M tokens。

还有一组容易被忽略的数据：可定制性。同样的数据和算法做后训练微调，Inkling 2 Small 学得比前代更快、终点更高——金融文档摘要任务上，75 步就到了 Inkling-Small 训到底的水平。对想用 Tinker 造自家垂直模型的企业客户，这可能比榜单分数更重要。

## 开放节奏：先闭门，下周开源

发布策略延续了官方那篇《a safe path to open weights》的路线：

- 今天：Tinker Playground 可直接试用；Tinker 上可微调、可采样（企业客户的老用法）；
- 下周：Apache 2.0 全权重开放，checkpoint 可下载——前提是外部安全测试和红队完成。

这个「先闭门跑安全测试、再放权重」的节奏在 Inkling-Small 时就用过，执行上没有跳票记录。当然「下周」是计划表述，具体哪天官方没承诺（uncertain，以官方公告为准）。

## 怎么看

几个观察角度：

- 594B/17B 的配置很精明：总参堆知识容量、激活控制推理成本，Apache 2.0 + 下周开源，摆明了要抢「自托管 + 微调」的企业市场——这正是 Tinker 的生意。
- 联合 RL 替代多教师蒸馏是训练工程上值得盯的信号：一锅端的联合 RL 如果真在各维度全面超过「分科训练再合并」，这个经验会很快被开源社区复用。
- NVFP4 原生预训练跑通（68 小时 GB300）意味着 4-bit 浮点已经从「推理量化格式」升级成「训练原生格式」，配合本文同日另一篇量化实测的结论看，硬件格式演进正在重塑训练-推理的成本曲线。
- 对普通开发者：等下周权重放出，594B 总参量化后能不能进消费级显存是另一个问题——17B 激活的 MoE 推理成本倒是可以期待。

一年时间从零到第二代 594B 模型，这家 2025 年初成立、还没发过产品的公司（Tinker 除外），节奏已经超过了不少老牌实验室。第二代的小杯先来，大杯（Inkling 2 正主）估计也不远了。

# Nace AI releases Drex technical report and 27B Drex Max decision model

The Palo Alto startup's flagship model scores 67.52 on Decision Index 0.4 with a median latency of roughly 183 milliseconds

Most AI models answer a question by writing. Nace AI wants its models to simply decide.

The Palo Alto startup has published a technical report titled “Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex” on arXiv, released around November 5, 2026. Alongside it comes Drex Max, a 27-billion-parameter model built to pick from a set of options rather than generate paragraphs of text.

The pitch is speed and cost. Nace AI says Drex Max hits a median response time of approximately 183 milliseconds. Comparable systems, by the company’s measure, take between 2 and 3.5 seconds to respond.

## What Drex Max actually does

Technically, the model returns calibrated outputs tied to those user-defined choices. It does this in a single forward pass instead of using the autoregressive approach common to chat-style models.

The model is also multimodal. Drex Max accepts text, images, JSON and video as inputs. It supports a 262,000-token context window.

On benchmarks, Drex Max scored 67.52 on Decision Index 0.4. Nace AI describes that result as a new state-of-the-art among decision models.

## How the models were trained

The technical report centers on how Nace AI trained the Drex family. The company used a method it calls RLAF, combined with supervised fine-tuning and consistency losses.

Drex Max is not the only release. The full Drex model family is available, including a smaller 9B variant. The models and associated resources are being distributed through GitHub and Hugging Face.

### AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

The family ships under the Nace.AI Open RAIL-M license.

## Background on Nace AI

Nace AI is a young company. It was founded in 2024 and is based in Palo Alto.

In May 2026, the startup raised $21.5 million in seed funding. Walden Catalyst led the round, with General Catalyst also participating.

The company has already been packaging its decision technology into specific products. Those include Drex for Search and Drex for Finance.

## What this means

The interesting bet here is architectural. Much of the AI industry has spent the past few years making models bigger and more conversational. Nace AI is arguing that a large share of enterprise work does not need conversation at all.

Calibration is the quieter selling point. In enterprise settings, knowing how confident a model is can matter as much as the answer itself.

The product lineup hints at the target customers. Drex for Finance suggests banks and financial firms, where latency and auditability both carry weight. Drex for Search suggests ranking and retrieval.

The open-release strategy is the other lever. Putting the full family, including the 9B variant, on GitHub and Hugging Face lowers the barrier for developers to test the approach.

The latency and benchmark comparisons come from Nace AI itself. Decision Index 0.4 is also a specialized benchmark. The license terms will shape adoption too, as Open RAIL-M style restrictions can limit some commercial uses.

# Announcing AI agent launchpad

Announced on | Rollout starts | Rollout ends 
---|---|---
November 5, 2026 | November 5, 2026 | November 30, 2026 

Zendesk is introducing AI agent launchpad, a guided experience designed to accelerate your setup, shorten time to value, and optimize performance across your AI agents.

This announcement includes the following topics:

## What is changing?

AI agent launchpad introduces new tools that use your business signals to take on more of the work behind building and growing AI agents - so you can get to value in minutes and unlock more automation over time.

Here's how it works:

- AI-guided onboarding: Instead of starting with a blank configuration, launchpad analyzes your account ticket history to detect common customer topics. It automatically generates and proposes procedures and help center articles, then tests your AI agent against high-impact scenarios to validate readiness before go-live.
- Agent overview page: Monitor performance for individual AI agents from a dedicated view. The overview provides key metrics including automated resolutions (AR), total conversation volume, and understood conversations, along with direct navigation to tone of voice, channel configuration, and knowledge sources.
- Tailored recommendations: AI agents continuously evaluates your ticket trends to surface suggestions for new generative procedures and help center articles. Admins can generate content in one click, save recommendations for later, or skip suggestions with contextual feedback to refine future suggestions.

For more details, see:

## Why is Zendesk making this change?

Deploying and tuning an AI agent traditionally requires substantial manual effort, from identifying user intent trends to authoring articles and testing workflows. AI agent launchpad eliminates this guesswork by grounding your agent configuration in actual ticket data, enabling you to deploy a fully tested AI agent in minutes and continuously improve automation rates over time.

## What do I need to do?

AI agent launchpad is available to customers on the latest AI agent infrastructure.

- New AI agents: When creating a messaging or email AI agent, follow the guided launchpad onboarding flow to generate initial topics, procedures, and articles. To learn more, see Creating an AI agent to automatically resolve customer issues.
- Existing AI agents: In the AI agents workspace, select an AI agent, click Optimize in the sidebar, and click Agent overview or Recommendations to review live metrics and suggested actions. To learn more, see Using the agent overview to monitor and manage a specific AI agent and Using tailored recommendations to automate manual tasks and optimize workflows in AI agents.

cross_cutting.title: It doesn't work. Yet.
cross_cutting.description: OpenAI released GPT-4 Turbo. ... The idea was an AI agent that could dig through it and answer real questions, the kind an analyst might spend a day on. ... When a new model came along, it "just worked", and it launched in July 2026.
cross_cutting.content:
# It doesn’t work. Yet.

Mintel's AI projects failed again and again, until one day they didn't. Why an AI idea that flopped last year deserves a second go.

Three days before launch, Mintel's new AI product didn't work.

The team had built a tool to answer questions over their research. It was 2023. The answers weren't good enough, and the launch date was fixed. OpenAI released GPT-4 Turbo. Three days later the product went out, and it worked.

Jason Thomson, who leads innovation at Mintel, told that story at aiblLIVE in London on 20 October. It was one of several on a slide he might as well have titled "not yet".

## Two and a half years of no

The best one was a database agent. Mintel runs GNPD, a huge database of product launches from around the world. The idea was an AI agent that could dig through it and answer real questions, the kind an analyst might spend a day on.

It failed, and failed again. For two and a half years, by Jason's account, it didn't work. When a new model came along, it "just worked", and it launched in July 2026.

His line, which every business owner should hear: "Often when they don't work, it's just that they don't work yet."

## Why it keeps changing

There's a reason for this, beyond the hype.

Epoch AI, a research group that tracks how AI is developing, published a study in September 2026. It found that the cost of getting a given level of AI performance has fallen about 47% every quarter for three years. That's around 13 times cheaper every year. Jason quoted an even bigger number on stage. Epoch's own figure is impressive enough.

When something gets that much cheaper and better that quickly, last year's "can't be done" is often this year's "of course".

## What changes when it works

Jason didn't run his demo live. Instead he showed a recording of the finished agent working through a question about high-protein fizzy products. By his account it ran 16 searches and 13 analyses over five years of product launches, in three minutes, and wrote four pages.

And he said the thing that stuck with me most. "Maybe 1 in 4 of our users could have done this analysis by hand, and those that could would only have bothered if it was a really important question."

And: "When something gets that much easier, it stops being the same thing." As he put it, "You get new questions asked."

That's the real prize. People ask questions they'd never have bothered with before, because the cost of asking has dropped to almost nothing.

## A list worth keeping

I like this idea because it fits something I've believed for a long time. Done beats perfect. You try, you learn, you go again. The bit people forget is the "go again".

Plenty of us try an AI tool once, get a so-so result and decide it's not for them. Some of that is fair. A lot of it is timing.

Here's a simple habit that helps. Keep a "not yet" list. Every time you try something with AI that doesn't quite work, a proposal, an analysis, a tidy-up of your customer list, write it down with the date. Every three months, try the top three again.

What matters is paying attention when "not yet" quietly becomes "now". That way you get there while everyone else is still telling each other it doesn't work.

Jason admitted the pace is tiring. "It's exhausting," he said in the Q&A, because what's possible "changes every week." He's right. A list makes it manageable. You don't have to chase every change, just check back on the things you already wanted. What's on your "not yet" list?

# From Free Trial to Paying Customer: How Startups Use AI Agents to Convert Trial Users

November 6, 2026

7 minutes

Vuk Dukic

Founder, Senior Software Engineer

Vuk Dukic is the founder of Anablock and a senior software engineer focused on building practical AI systems, automation, and digital products for real business operations.

# From Free Trial to Paying Customer: How Startups Use AI Agents to Convert Trial Users

Your trial sign ups look healthy. The dashboard says 400 new accounts this month. Then you check how many reached the one action that proves your product works, and the number is a fraction of that.

This is the quiet leak at the center of most startups. Acquisition gets the budget, the launch posts, and the team attention. Meanwhile most trial users sign up, poke around for a few minutes, get distracted, and never come back.

Free trial conversion is rarely lost in a single dramatic moment. It is lost in small ones: a confusing first screen, a setup step that stalls, a week of silence, a decision that gets made on day 13 with no one in the room.

The good news is that those moments are predictable. And that makes them perfect for AI agents.

## Why trial users do not convert

Trial users are not rejecting your product. Most of them never got far enough to form an opinion. The common causes are simple:

- They never reached value. They signed up with a problem in mind, but the path from the welcome screen to the first useful result was longer than their patience.
- They got stuck and stayed quiet. Most stuck users do not file a support ticket. They just leave.
- They forgot. A trial is a low priority for a busy person. Without a reason to return, other work wins.
- They hit the deadline without a plan. If the first real conversation about pricing happens on the last day, the answer is usually no.

A small team cannot watch every trial user personally. A well designed AI agent can.

## What product led growth AI actually means

Product led growth works because the product itself does the selling. Users experience value first, then pay. The weakness is that it assumes users find the value on their own.

Product led growth AI closes that gap. Instead of a fixed email drip that sends the same messages to everyone on the same days, an AI agent reads what each user actually did and responds to it. Think of it as a loop with four parts:

- Observe. Track product events such as account created, integration connected, first project made, teammate invited.
- Decide. Compare each user's progress with the path that leads to paid conversion, and spot where they are falling behind.
- Act. Send the right message, in the right channel, at the right moment, written for that user's situation.
- Hand off. When a user shows strong buying signals or hits a problem the agent cannot solve, route them to a human right away.

That last step matters. The goal is not to replace your team. It is to point your team at the users who most need a person.

## Day 1: Get to the first win

The first session decides more than any other. A user who reaches a meaningful result on day 1 is far more likely to return than one who only finishes a profile.

Define your activation moment first. It is the specific action that correlates with long term use. For a CRM, it might be importing contacts and sending a first message. For an analytics tool, it might be connecting a data source and viewing a first chart.

Then build the day 1 agent around that single goal:

- Ask one question at sign up. What are you trying to do? The answer lets the agent personalize everything that follows.
- Send a welcome that points to one next step. Not five links. One clear action tied to the stated goal.
- Offer help inside the product. An AI assistant that answers setup questions in plain language removes the most common reason for early exits.
- Do part of the work for the user. Preload sample data, draft a first template, or complete an integration step on their behalf.

The test is simple. If a user spends ten minutes with your product on day 1, they should leave having seen something that worked.

## Day 5: Catch stalled usage

By the middle of the trial, the pattern splits. Some users are active and exploring. Others have gone quiet, and these are the ones you can still save.

Stalled usage is a signal, and an agent can read it the moment it appears. Useful triggers include:

- No login for 48 hours after sign up
- Setup started but not finished
- The activation moment still not reached by day 5
- A key feature never opened

The response should match the trigger. A user who abandoned setup halfway needs a short message that names the exact step where they stopped and offers to finish it with them. A user who logged in but never touched the core feature needs a quick walkthrough of that feature, tied to the goal they gave on day 1.

Keep these nudges useful, not noisy. One message that solves a specific problem beats three that say "just checking in." And if the user still does not respond, let the agent change channels or try a different angle instead of repeating itself.

This is also the point to ask a direct question. Something like "What got in the way?" often gets a reply, and the answer teaches your team more about your onboarding than any dashboard.

## Day 12: Support the decision

By day 12, the user is deciding, whether they say so or not. This is where many startups go silent, then send a generic "your trial ends soon" notice that reads like an alarm.

A better day 12 agent does three things.

It summarizes the value already created. A message that says what the user accomplished, such as contacts imported, messages sent, or hours saved, makes the case for paying better than any pitch.

It answers the pricing question before it is asked. Show which plan fits their usage and what changes after the trial. Remove surprises, and the decision gets easier.

It routes high intent users to a human. If a user invited teammates, hit a usage limit, or visited the pricing page more than once, those are buying signals. This is the moment for a person to step in with a short call, not another automated email.

For users who did not engage, the day 12 message can offer an extension or a quick conversation about what was missing. A short extension for an engaged but busy user often converts better than letting the trial lapse.

## SaaS onboarding automation: the building blocks

You do not need a huge stack to start. SaaS onboarding automation with AI agents rests on a few essentials:

- Clean event data. The agent can only react to what it can see. Make sure key actions are tracked and tied to each user.
- A defined activation path. Know what success looks like in the first 14 days, and the milestones along the way.
- A connected customer record. Product activity, emails, conversations, and notes should live in one place so the agent and your team see the same story.
- Guardrails. Set limits on how often an agent can message a user, what it can offer, and when it must hand off to a person.
- Human review at the start. Approve the first batches of messages, learn what works, then loosen the controls gradually.

## How to measure whether it works

Track a short list of numbers and review them weekly:

- Activation rate. The share of trial users who reach the activation moment.
- Time to first value. How long it takes from sign up to that moment.
- Trial to paid conversion. The headline number, broken down by the path each user took.
- Response rate to nudges. Which messages and channels actually get replies.
- Handoff quality. How often users routed to your team turn into paying customers.

If activation goes up, conversion usually follows. Fix the early steps first.

## Mistakes to avoid

- Automating a broken onboarding. An agent cannot rescue a confusing product. Fix the biggest friction points first.
- Sending too much. More messages do not mean more conversions. Relevance does.
- Hiding the human. Make it easy for users to reach a real person when they want one.
- Ignoring privacy. Be clear about what data you use, and respect opt outs and local rules on messaging.
- Measuring only the end. Conversion is the result. Activation is the lever.

At Anablock, we build AI agents and an AI first CRM that work together to turn early interest into revenue. Ana, the AI assistant inside Anablock CRM, can qualify leads, draft and send outreach, schedule follow up sequences, and keep every contact and conversation in one record. Echo handles conversations across channels and passes the right people to your team. Together they give a lean startup team the coverage of a much larger one, without losing the personal touch that closes deals.

If your trial numbers look good but your paid numbers do not, there is probably a leak in the first 14 days. We can help you find it and build the agents that close it.

# Brookfield, NAVER Form $9 Billion AI Data Center Partnership in Korea

Next-Generation Nvidia Chips to Be Brought In Buildout to Proceed in Phases From Next Year NAVER Cloud to Operate the Facilities

Lee Chung-hee·Published2026-11-06 14:24 KST

Brookfield, the global alternative asset manager, said on the 6th that it has signed a $9 billion (about 12.2 trillion won) investment agreement with NAVER (035420.KS). Brookfield will deploy the funds to build next-generation Nvidia computing infrastructure in South Korea.

Under the agreement, Brookfield will finance more than 200 megawatts of Nvidia GPU infrastructure to be installed across multiple data centers in the country, and will own the assets directly. NAVER Cloud, a wholly owned subsidiary of NAVER, will secure the entire computing capacity of the data centers under a long-term contract and will operate them. The buildout will proceed in phases from next year through 2028.

Brookfield said the transaction is the largest sponsor-led private investment ever made in South Korea. It also marks Brookfield's first investment in AI computing infrastructure in the country.

The investment is part of a strategic partnership announced in July by Brookfield, NAVER and Nvidia. The three companies aim to accelerate the development of South Korea's AI infrastructure in response to rising demand for advanced computing capacity from both companies and governments.

Sikander Rashid, global head of AI infrastructure at Brookfield, said AI infrastructure is entering a new phase. "The ability to deliver capital and computing capacity at scale to meet rising demand will be more critical than ever," he said. He added that the deal shows Brookfield can bring together long-term institutional capital, capabilities in developing and operating AI infrastructure, and strategic partners to speed up the buildout of core AI infrastructure.

Park Joon-woo, head of Brookfield's Korea operations, said South Korea is a market with a solid technology ecosystem and some of the world's most innovative companies. "This investment with NAVER and Nvidia reflects our conviction in the long-term growth potential of the Korean market, as well as our commitment to actively supporting the infrastructure that will underpin Korea's next generation of innovation," he said. He stressed that Brookfield is not merely a provider of funds but a long-term strategic partner that combines capital, industrial expertise and a global network to help companies grow.

# Expression of Interest: Establishment of an Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group

## Executive Summary

The Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science (DFHERIS) invites Expressions of Interest from experts in research and industry to join the newly established ‘Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group’. Public sector representatives will be nominated by their respective organisations.

The Group will bring together stakeholders from government, academia, industry and the wider user community to help shape Ireland's AI and high-performance computing (HPC) landscape. Members will provide strategic advice on national priorities, foster collaboration across key initiatives, support the development of a national roadmap for HPC and AI infrastructure, and help maximise the impact of public investment for economic, scientific and societal benefit.

## Background

As a small but highly innovative economy, Ireland's ability to compete internationally depends on its capacity to bring together stakeholders around shared priorities.

Ireland is entering a period of significant investments and activity in digital infrastructure, including:

- The launch of the AI Factory Antenna in July 2026.
- The ongoing procurement process for the Caspir High-Performance Computing (HPC) supercomputer.
- Commitment of €10 million to the European AI Gigafactories initiative.
- Forthcoming initiatives under the CASPIr programme.

To maximise the benefits of a cohesive digital ecosystem, structure and coordination mechanisms are required.

It is therefore proposed to set up a ‘HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group’ with responsibility for reviewing initiatives, assessing gaps and opportunities, and identifying multipliers.

## Purpose of the Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group

The Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group would provide a structured platform to:

- Support the development of a strategic approach to existing and future digital infrastructure investments.
- Provide expert advice to a novel National Advanced Computing Strategy, in alignment with broader national digital policy objectives. This Strategy will provide a national roadmap towards Ireland’s digital maturity, with long-term plans covering hardware, capacities and strategic elements.
- Review Ireland's digital infrastructure activities in a comprehensive and coordinated manner, identifying synergies, overlaps, and opportunities for collaboration.
- Give feedback to novel programmes or initiatives as appropriate, ensuring that all sectors’ perspectives are fully considered.
- Ensure that perspectives from government, industry, academia, and the wider user community are represented in national discussions.
- Advise on national benefits related to international activities and opportunities.
- Facilitate the dissemination of relevant information, opportunities, and strategic developments to stakeholders across academic and non-academic sectors. That would maximise the uptake of public-funded infrastructure, enhancing their value for money and widespread benefit.
- Identify key stakeholders, champions, and multipliers who can strengthen connections across the Irish digital infrastructure ecosystem.

For reference, draft Terms of Reference included here.

HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group Terms of Reference

View the file View

## Group membership

The ‘Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group’ will be chaired by DFHERIS with members drawn from research, public sector, and industry. This latter should encompass both multinationals and endogenous business, ranging from large-scale companies to promising startups.

Public sector representatives will be nominated by their organisations while representatives from research and industry will be selected through this call of interest.

## How to Apply

Expressions of interest are now invited from suitably qualified candidates who wish to be considered for membership of group.
To express your interest, please complete submit a CV (max 2 pages) and a cover letter (max 500 words) no later than December 3rd.

Together, these documents should clearly outline:

- Your areas of expertise;
- Your current role;
- A brief career biography.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by email to the following address: rpp@dfheris.gov.ie by the deadline stated above. The subject line needs to be: ‘Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group _FIRST NAME LAST NAME’.

Participation in the group as member is voluntary and unremunerated.

### Additional Information

In line with best practice, as set out in the Guidelines on Appointments to State Boards, the Minister reserves the right to consider other suitable nominees outside of this process.
The Minister may also take into account the importance of diversity and gender balance when making appointments to the forum.

## Decision on group membership

All expressions of interest will be acknowledged within three working days of receipt.

The Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science will review all expressions received and will recommend the composition of the group to the Minister, having regard to the purpose of the group as outlined above.

## What we do with your information

By making an expression of interest to this call, you are confirming your acceptance of the below terms.

### Freedom of information

Responses to this consultation are subject to the provisions of the Freedom of Information Act 2014. Read how to make a freedom of information request.

### Data protection

Any personal information submitted to the Department will be treated strictly in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation 2016/67 and the Data Protection Act 2018. Read the Department’s data protection notice.

### Purpose

Your data is processed to receive expressions of interest from interested candidates for membership of the Irish HPC and AI Public Infrastructure Advisory Group and maintain contact.

### Legal basis

Processing your data is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest.

### Categories of data subject

This is a public invitation for expressions of interest: anyone may make a submission, either in a personal or representative capacity.

### Categories of personal data

- Name
- Email address

### Further processing

Where the Department intends to further process your data for a purpose other than the purposes listed above, the Department will provide you prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information on the processing activity and your data protection rights.

### Storage period

The data processed will be retained for a period of up to one year for the purpose of completing the appointment process.

Please note that your data is also subject to the National Archives Act 1986, see guidance from the National Archives.

### Third country

None of your data will be transferred to a country outside of the European Economic Area, which is:

- the EU
- Norway
- Iceland
- Liechtenstein

### Data subject rights

Read information on your right to access your data. You may also exercise your right to correct your data, seek to restrict how it may be processed or object to how it may be processed. Your data or that or your child’s will not be used for automated decision-making or profiling. Read the Data Protection Commissioner’s guide to data subject rights.

While you have a right to have your data deleted, the Department may not be able to agree to your request if it is less than 3 years since you submitted your application under this expression of interest. The Department may not be able to agree to your request for deletion also where your data is subject to the National Archives Act 1986 and no order has been made to dispose of the this category of data under that Act, see guidance from the National Archives.

## How to complain

You have the right to lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Commission.

# Fermaca to deploy 60MW of AI capacity in Mexico with Nvidia by 2027

Bnamericas Published: Friday, November 06, 2026

Mexican group Fermaca launched an artificial intelligence factory platform based on Nvidia technology, through which it expects to reach 60MW of power in operational facilities by the end of 2027.

The first deployment, Fermaca Digital Origins, will be located in Mexico City and will include an initial cluster of Nvidia B300 NVL72 systems, part of the Blackwell Ultra generation launched by Nvidia in 2025.

The roadmap calls for later incorporating the Vera Rubin platform, Blackwell’s successor, with first shipments scheduled by Nvidia for the second half of 2026. The companies did not disclose the number of GPUs acquired or when the cluster will start operating.

The 60MW target refers to the facilities’ total power and has a deadline of December 31, 2027, the company said.

Fermaca claims to be the first Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) headquartered in Mexico. Taiwan’s Inventec will supply the computing systems and US-based DDN, which specializes in data storage, will handle storage. Fermaca, for its part, will be responsible for developing and operating the infrastructure.

The platform targets companies, universities, institutions, developers and research centers in Mexico and Latin America, with the stated goal of strengthening digital sovereignty, according to the company.

“Fermaca is investing in Mexico’s capacity to produce intelligence,” said Manuel Calvillo Gandara, project coordinator at Fermaca Infraestructura. “Our ambition runs from gas molecule to token.”

The company seeks to combine its gas infrastructure and energy development with fiber optic connectivity, AI facilities and accelerated computing.

“We’re excited to support Mexico’s growing AI ecosystem,” said Márcio Aguiar, director of Nvidia’s enterprise division for Latin America.

Fermaca said it has the support of federal, state and municipal authorities, in line with Plan México. The initiative also includes the México Aprende IA con Fermaca y NVIDIA program, which will train university professors in AI, starting in Durango.

Investments in Durango

Over the longer term, the platform includes Fermaca Digital City, in Durango, where the company aims to reach up to 1GW of IT capacity. According to Fermaca, this is a separate milestone from the 60MW target, since IT capacity measures computing equipment only.

In April, the Durango state congress approved the donation of 50ha within the Durango industrial logistics center (CLID) to Fermaca Digital for the Fermaca data center, which envisages up to 250MW of capacity, estimated investment of US$2.7bn and the creation of 1,000 direct jobs.

The complex also includes a gas pipeline branch from Texas, a combined cycle plant to power the data center and a fiber optic network.

Through its subsidiary Fermachem, the group is also developing a fertilizer plant in the municipality of Lerdo, Durango, which will require an investment of 28bn pesos (US$1.6bn), according to the state government.

In June, Fermaca signed an engineering services agreement with Spain’s Técnicas Reunidas for the project, which will produce around 1Mt/y of urea and is expected to start operating in 2029.

Natural gas for the plant will be supplied by Esentia Energy Systems, a pipeline operator in which Fermaca is a shareholder.

(The original version of this content was written in Spanish)

# Kakao Enterprise partners with Mongolia on cloud technology, cultivates local talent

- Input
- 2026-11-06 17:17:34

- Updated
- 2026-11-06 17:17:34

[Financial News] Kakao Enterprise is stepping up its push into overseas markets by supporting the development of Mongolia’s cloud infrastructure and the training of skilled professionals. Its strategy is to showcase its technological competitiveness through cooperation with the local government and universities and expand its influence in Mongolia’s cloud market.

According to industry sources on the 6th, Kakao Enterprise held a joint industry-academia-government cloud technology workshop at the Mongolian University of Science and Technology on the 5th (local time).

The event was organized as part of the ‘KOICA Platform Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Initiative,’ a collaborative project that Kakao Enterprise has been pursuing with the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) over three years since 2024.

The KOICA Platform ESG Initiative is a public-private partnership program that supports economic and social development in developing countries by linking companies’ environmental, social and governance (ESG) activities with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Around 80 people, including representatives from the Mongolian government, the information technology (IT) industry and academia, attended the workshop. Across eight sessions, they discussed plans for Mongolia’s transition to public cloud, data center operations and the development of a cloud industry ecosystem.

During the morning session, B. Davapurev, head of technology at Mongolia’s National Data Center (NDC), presented plans for the transition to public cloud. Lee Seung, a manager on Kakao Enterprise’s IaaS Core Development Team, then introduced cloud development and validation technologies using artificial intelligence (AI).

Kakao Enterprise uses technology that creates a private cloud environment on a single server identical to the actual production environment. This enables developers and AI agents to test changes to cloud systems in advance and apply them to live services after validation.

The manager explained, “Cloud infrastructure involves many interconnected layers, including application programming interfaces (APIs), virtual networks and physical equipment, making development and validation very challenging. KakaoCloud creates a private cloud environment on a single server that is identical to the actual production environment, allowing developers and AI agents to validate changes in advance and then deploy them safely.”

Presentations and discussions were also held on topics including disaster recovery (DR) systems for Mongolia’s private-sector cloud services, the development of future digital infrastructure and the creation of a cloud industry ecosystem.

Through this collaborative project, Kakao Enterprise has built an edge cloud test environment with the Mongolian University of Science and Technology and has been training local cloud specialists. Edge cloud is a technology that processes data close to where it is generated.
